display_title: Add `stablehlo.fma` op to StableHLO and VHLO 1.24.0.

head_commit.message:
Add `stablehlo.fma` op to StableHLO and VHLO 1.24.0.

`stablehlo.fma` (`vhlo.fma_v1`) computes the single-rounded IEEE-754 `fusedMultiplyAdd(a, b, c)` result (`llvm.fma` semantics). It cannot be downgraded below VHLO 1.24.0 because `add(multiply(a, b), c)` rounds twice and would break its single-rounding guarantee.

Implement reference interpreter evaluation, constant folding in `StablehloAggressiveFolder`, Linalg/Arith scalar lowering, documentation, and temporary MHLO legalizer stubs.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Hoist dynamic slice offsets out of concatenate regions

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Hoist dynamic slice offsets out of concatenate regions

In tiling, concatenate branches are hoisting barriers, so a
dynamic slice that is reachable from several branches gets its offsets tiled in
each of them. However, `rt_symbol_to_tiled_hlo` maps each runtime variable to a
single tiled instruction (the one from the first branch), and the emitter uses
it in all branches, where it does not dominate its uses:

  error: operand #1 does not dominate this use

Runtime variables are scalars that do not depend on the tile, so hoist them out
of conditional regions too.

HLO diff can report matched instructions that are unchanged themselves but used
differently (e.g. swapped operands) as moved instead of unchanged. The
comparison manager and the original tensor summary comparator only mapped

still tile these concatenates. GEMM fusion keeps requiring 64-aligned concatenate operands.

name: CI
display_title: Let PjRt OOM errors carry the reason why memory ran out.

head_commit.message:
Let PjRt OOM errors carry the reason why memory ran out.

`SetOomErrorWithPayload()` marks out-of-memory errors with an empty `pjrt.OOM` payload, so callers can tell that an operation ran out of memory, but not why: for example, whether the request was larger than the free memory or the free memory was too fragmented.

Add a required `OomReason` (`kOutOfMemory`, `kFragmentation` or `kUnknown`) to `SetOomErrorWithPayload()`, stored as the payload's value, and `GetOomErrorReason()` to read it back. `HasOomErrorPayload()` is unaffected.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1003566646

name: CI
display_title: Fix base dilation overlap in SpaceToBatchConverter

head_commit.message:
Fix base dilation overlap in SpaceToBatchConverter

When inherent_low_padding equals base_dilation_factor, SpaceToBatchConverter prepends one undilated element to each split and sets low_padding_for_conv to 0.

For each split of S undilated elements to produce S * base_dilation_factor outputs, the high-side overlap must be kernel_spatial_dim_size + base_dilation_factor - 2 rather than kernel_spatial_dim_size (which only matched for base_dilation_factor == 2). Therefore this change updates last_overlap in GetConvolutionDetails accordingly.

Fixes https://github.com/openxla/xla/issues/51365

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1004178625

display_title: Deprecate `tsl::strings::LegacyPrecision` in favor of `absl::HighPrecision`.

head_commit.message:
Deprecate `tsl::strings::LegacyPrecision` in favor of `absl::HighPrecision`.

`LegacyPrecision(float)` and `LegacyPrecision(double)` now forward to
`absl::HighPrecision`, and the custom `FpToBuffer` implementation is removed.

This is a value-preserving but not byte-identical change in formatting:
- float: the old implementation used %.6g and fell back to %.9g. absl uses
  the shortest of 6-9 significant digits that round-trips, e.g.
  1.17549435e-38f is now printed as "1.1754944e-38". This matches what the
  header comment already documented (%.6g, %.7g, %.8g, or %.9g).
- double: unchanged (%.15g, falling back to %.17g).
- NaN with the sign bit set is now printed as "nan" instead of "-nan".

All outputs still round-trip to the exact same value.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1003771966

name: CI
display_title: [XLA:CPU] Lower log and log1p to YNNPACK SIMD bitcode kernels

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU] Lower log and log1p to YNNPACK SIMD bitcode kernels

Replaces the XLA:CPU implementations of `log` and `log1p` in the MLIR fusion
pipeline with YNNPACK SIMD kernels compiled to LLVM bitcode via `cc_to_llvm_ir`:

- Compile YNNPACK SIMD `log` and `log1p` kernels for 128-bit, 256-bit (AVX2),
  and 512-bit (AVX-512) vector targets into embedded LLVM bitcode.
- Support single-precision (`f32`, `v2f32`, `v4f32`, `v8f32`, `v16f32`) and
  double-precision (`f64`, `v2f64`, `v4f64`, `v8f64`) types.
- F16 and BF16 continue to upcast to F32 via the existing
  `LowerXlaIntrinsicLibPass` infrastructure.
- Preserve signed zero for `log1p(-0.0) = -0.0` via `copysign`.
- Upcast F16/BF16 `log1p` to F32 in the CPU elemental emitter (used for small
  while loops), since the YNNPACK `log1p` kernels have no F16 variant.
- Windows (where bitcode embedding is disabled) and GPU continue to use `libm`
  and handwritten `log1p` lowering.
- Relax the JAX CPU float64 `log` accuracy bound (and `docs/accuracy.md`) to
  1.5 ULP, matching NVIDIA GPU; it previously assumed a correctly rounded
  `libm` `log`.
- Tighten the JAX CPU float32 `log1p` bound from 3.0 to 2.5 ULP (exhaustive max
  2.16 ULP).
- Relax tolerances in TF tests that compare XLA against `numpy` at 1-2 ULP:
  float64 `geomspace` in `np_test` (to `1e-14`, as for `complex128`) and
  float32 `Log1pTest` on CPU (to `2.5e-7`, as on GPU).
- Remove `GenerateVF32Log` from `polynomial_approximations.cc` while retaining
  `GenerateVF32Exp`.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 990490468

name: CI
display_title: [XLA:CPU] Run post-layout simplification before fusion

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU] Run post-layout simplification before fusion

`AlgebraicSimplifier` only visits non-fusion computations. Running it after
`CpuInstructionFusion` and `FusionWrapper` meant that bitcast-equivalent copies
and reshapes left by `LayoutAssignment` (for example around LAPACK custom calls)
were wrapped into loop fusions instead of becoming bitcasts. Move the
simplification pipeline before fusion and drop the second `FusionWrapper`, which
only existed to wrap elementwise ops created by the late simplification.

Running the simplifier before fusion exposed two latent bugs, fixed here:

*   `AlgebraicSimplifier`: the `bitcast(unary(bitcast(x)))` rewrite treated
    `kCopy` as a pure elementwise op and dropped the layout change it performs.
*   `ElementalIrEmitter`: a fused `kBitcast` that changes the element type
    forwarded the operand value without an LLVM bitcast.

Context: https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/33666
PiperOrigin-RevId: 1003497443

name: CI
display_title: Speed up Clang-Tidy, DWYU, and query CI workflows

head_commit.message:
Speed up Clang-Tidy, DWYU, and query CI workflows

The Clang-Tidy, DWYU, and Bazel query/lint workflows in GitHub Actions currently repeat full-repository analysis or force actions to run locally on the runner VM:

1. In `clang_tidy.yml` and `run_clang_tidy.sh`, GPU `xla_test` targets inherit `tags = ["local"]` from `gpu_test_tags()`, which Bazel propagates to the `ClangTidy` aspect actions. That forces `clang-tidy` to download the hermetic LLVM toolchain and execute locally instead of on RBE. In addition, `xla_test` expands into up to 10 backend `cc_test` variants that compile the same sources, `bazel build` discards the `bazel cquery` analysis cache because `build:rbe_base --test_env=USER=anon` and `build:cuda` are not applied to `cquery`, and `bazel run //build_tools/ci:clang_tidy_diff` triggers a third Bazel analysis pass and downloads `@llvm20_linux_x86_64//:all` even when `--fix` is not set.
2. In `dwyu.yml`, the workflow fetches all branches (`fetch-depth: 0`) and runs `bazelisk build --nobuild //xla/...` across all XLA packages before running `check_dwyu.py` to see whether any C++ targets were even modified.
3. In `bazel_dependency_violations.yml`, `bazel_query.yml`, and `bazel_tags.yml`, each job runs `bazel build --nobuild //xla/...` before running `bazel cquery` or `bazel query //xla/...`, which analyzes the entire repository a second time (or runs full configured-target analysis when `bazel query` only needs package loading).

Therefore this change:

1. Strips `local` from `ClangTidy` actions (`--modify_execution_info=ClangTidy=-local`), deduplicates `xla_test` backend variants in `run_clang_tidy.sh`, aligns `rbe_base` and `cuda` flags under `common:` so `bazel build` reuses the `cquery` analysis cache, and runs `clang_tidy_diff.py` directly with `python3` when `--fix` is not enabled.
2. Checks out with `fetch-depth: 100` in `dwyu.yml`, runs `check_dwyu.py` before installing `bant`/`bazelisk` so PRs without modified C++ targets exit immediately, and scopes `bazelisk build --nobuild` to the packages of the modified targets rather than `//xla/...`.
3. Removes the redundant `bazel build --nobuild //xla/...` step from `bazel_dependency_violations.yml`, `bazel_query.yml`, and `bazel_tags.yml` (downloader retries are already handled by `--experimental_repository_downloader_retries=5`), and skips the `bazel cquery` step in `bazel_dependency_violations.yml` on PRs that do not touch `BUILD`, `.bzl`, `WORKSPACE`, `MODULE.bazel`, or `.bazelrc` files.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1004134421

display_title: [XLA:CPU] Lower log and log1p to YNNPACK SIMD bitcode kernels

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU] Lower log and log1p to YNNPACK SIMD bitcode kernels

Replaces the XLA:CPU implementations of `log` and `log1p` in the MLIR fusion
pipeline with YNNPACK SIMD kernels compiled to LLVM bitcode via `cc_to_llvm_ir`:

- Compile YNNPACK SIMD `log` and `log1p` kernels for 128-bit, 256-bit (AVX2),
  and 512-bit (AVX-512) vector targets into embedded LLVM bitcode.
- Support single-precision (`f32`, `v2f32`, `v4f32`, `v8f32`, `v16f32`) and
  double-precision (`f64`, `v2f64`, `v4f64`, `v8f64`) types.
- F16 and BF16 continue to upcast to F32 via the existing
  `LowerXlaIntrinsicLibPass` infrastructure.
- Preserve signed zero for `log1p(-0.0) = -0.0` via `copysign`.
- Upcast F16/BF16 `log1p` to F32 in the CPU elemental emitter (used for small
  while loops), since the YNNPACK `log1p` kernels have no F16 variant.
- Windows (where bitcode embedding is disabled) and GPU continue to use `libm`
  and handwritten `log1p` lowering.
- Relax the JAX CPU float64 `log` accuracy bound to 1.5 ULP; it previously
  assumed a correctly rounded `libm` `log`.
- Remove `GenerateVF32Log` from `polynomial_approximations.cc` while retaining
  `GenerateVF32Exp`.

display_title: [XLA] Check element types for kConvert in FloatSupport::EffectiveOperandPrecisionIsOutputPrecision.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Check element types for kConvert in FloatSupport::EffectiveOperandPrecisionIsOutputPrecision.

Make `FloatSupport::EffectiveOperandPrecisionIsOutputPrecision` a `const` member method and restrict `HloOpcode::kConvert` to same-type converts or transitions between `low_precision_type_` and `high_precision_type_`. Previously `kConvert` unconditionally returned `true`, which treated narrowing or unrelated converts (such as `F32 -> S32` or `F32 -> F16` under `BF16`/`F32` propagation) as preserving operand precision.

Same-type `kConvert` (`in_type == out_type`) is explicitly allowed because `BFloat16Propagation::RunImpl` inserts temporary `F32 -> F32` `kConvert` copies on `kWhile` inputs before running dataflow analysis to break buffer aliasing with external users. During the forward and backward propagation passes, proposed `BF16` demotions are recorded in `changes_to_bf16_` while the HLO instructions themselves remain `F32 -> F32` in the module until `MaterializeResolvedPrecisions` and `SkipNoopConversions` run at the end of the pass, so `AllUsersConsumeBF16` and `AddEdgesForUse` require `EffectiveOperandPrecisionIsOutputPrecision` to return `true` on those same-type converts.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Hoist dynamic slice offsets out of concatenate regions

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Hoist dynamic slice offsets out of concatenate regions

In the experimental tiling, concatenate branches are hoisting barriers, so a
dynamic slice that is reachable from several branches gets its offsets tiled in
each of them. However, `rt_symbol_to_tiled_hlo` maps each runtime variable to a
single tiled instruction (the one from the first branch), and the emitter uses
it in all branches, where it does not dominate its uses:

  error: operand #1 does not dominate this use

Runtime variables are scalars that do not depend on the tile, so hoist them out
of conditional regions too.

display_title: PR #51216: Reclaim unused regions in growing PJRT GPU memory pools

head_commit.message:
PR #51216: Reclaim unused regions in growing PJRT GPU memory pools

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51216

## 📝 Summary of Changes

Enable BFC's existing whole-free-region reclamation for PJRT GPU pools when `preallocate=false`, honoring `TF_ENABLE_GPU_GARBAGE_COLLECTION` with a default of `true`. Preallocated pools keep their reservation behavior. Gate the allocator test dependency behind `if_google` because OSS `xla_cc_test` adds it automatically.

## 🎯 Justification

Growing pools can retain separate, wholly free backing regions that cannot satisfy a larger request. When the remaining growth allowance is too small, allocation fails even though reclaiming those regions would permit the request within the configured cap. This affected Gemma2-9B and Gemma3-4B training.

The fix enables the existing reclaim-and-retry path without moving live allocations or raising the cap. The environment override makes the opt-out advertised by BFC's reclamation warning effective for PJRT pools. It does not address true capacity exhaustion or fragmentation within regions containing live allocations.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix · 🧪 Tests

## 📊 Benchmark

No performance improvement claim; earlier workload validation checked successful execution and finite losses.

## 🧪 Unit Tests

- Eight GPU-independent cases cover reclamation with the setting unset/enabled/disabled, live-allocation and capacity preservation, preallocated-pool retention, and invalid settings; existing upstream sizing tests are preserved.
- The earlier revision passed 59 allocator tests and failed the reclamation regression without the fix. This rebased revision passes formatting, whitespace, and static dependency checks; compilation and tests were not rerun because compute resources were unavailable.

## 🧪 Execution Tests

- Earlier manual four-GPU Gemma2-9B and Gemma3-4B training runs each completed 101 steps with finite losses, with recomputation enabled and disabled; these were not rerun for this revision. No automated execution tests were added.
- Both modes used the same earlier runtime with the fix applied, without a separate pre-fix baseline; the Gemma2 enabled run exercised profiling but did not accept the recomputation rewrite.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Dispatch custom host memory allocator unmap_fn on GPU 0 async dispatch thread.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Dispatch custom host memory allocator unmap_fn on GPU 0 async dispatch thread.

When a custom HostMemoryAllocator is configured on StreamExecutorGpuClient, allocator_options.map_fn registers host memory with CU_MEMHOSTREGISTER_PORTABLE on first_executor (GPU 0, primary context ctx_0), making the allocation portable across all CUDA contexts in the process. When allocator_options.unmap_fn later calls cuMemHostUnregister (first_executor->HostMemoryUnregister(data)), the CUDA driver acquires ctx_0's context write lock and synchronizes ctx_0 (which on B300+ also drains peer GPU streams recorded in ctx_0's cross-context stream semaphore list when touching portable memory, and on pre-B300 synchronizes peer contexts directly).

If unmap_fn runs on a background thread concurrently with a multi-GPU execution in ExecuteThunks (for example, inside a WhileThunk loop), a 3-way deadlock cycle can occur between host-side CUDA context locking and device-side collective synchronization:
1. Peer GPUs (GPU 1..N-1) enqueue their collective kernel (along with a tracked portable transfer or stream dependency) slightly ahead of GPU 0; on the device, the collective kernel on GPU 1..N-1 blocks waiting for GPU 0 to launch its corresponding collective kernel.
2. Before GPU 0 launches its collective kernel, a background thread calls cuMemHostUnregister, acquires ctx_0's context write lock, and spins inside the driver waiting for the in-flight streams to drain.
3. GPU 0's async_dispatch_thread attempts to launch GPU 0's collective kernel (e.g. cuLaunchKernelEx / cuStreamBeginCapture_v2 / cuEventRecord) and blocks on ctx_0's context lock behind cuMemHostUnregister.

With RendezvousAfterExecutableStart (cl/1002405325), peer GPUs cannot advance past the start of ExecuteThunks of a subsequent executable until GPU 0 has also entered it. Scheduling first_executor->HostMemoryUnregister(data) onto GPU 0's async_dispatch_thread() in unmap_fn ensures that cuMemHostUnregister only runs between executables—after GPU 0 has already enqueued all collective kernels for prior executables, and before any peer GPU can enqueue collective kernels for subsequent executables.

To keep `unmap_fn` safe during reentrant calls from any `async_dispatch_thread` and during client teardown:
- Add `WorkerThread::IsCurrentThread()` using `tsl::Env::GetCurrentThreadId()`.
- Capture pointers to the devices' `async_dispatch_threads` in `unmap_fn`, scheduling onto GPU 0's `async_dispatch_thread` and falling back to calling `HostMemoryUnregister` inline when already running on any device's `async_dispatch_thread`.
- Extract `LocalDeviceState::DestroyStreams()` to drain scheduling threads, synchronize activity, destroy streams, and drain callback/cleanup threads while keeping the worker threads alive until `~LocalDeviceState()`.
- In `~PjRtStreamExecutorRawClient()`, drain `async_dispatch_thread` and `execute_thread` on all local devices, reset `async_work_runner_`, call `DestroyStreams()` on all local devices, and then reset `host_memory_allocator_` before `local_device_states_` is destroyed so all in-flight host staging buffers are released and any cached buffers unmapped in `~HostMemoryAllocator()` can still dispatch onto `async_dispatch_thread`.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Normalize dot batch dimensions only when cuBLAS cannot handle the layout.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Normalize dot batch dimensions only when cuBLAS cannot handle the layout.

1. Problem: cuBLAS natively supports multiple batch dimensions when physically
   sequential (which layout assignment ensures), yet GemmRewriter always
   collapsed them.
   Solution: Skip batch normalization when MatrixLayout accepts the layouts.

2. Problem: When normalization is needed (e.g. after SplitkRewriter),
   GemmRewriter only merged 2 batch dimensions and emitted reshapes that failed
   in the fission autotuner.
   Solution: Merge all batch dimensions into one, bitcasting when possible and
   transposing to default layout otherwise.

3. Problem: IsCublasSupportedMatMul rejected logically last batch dimensions
   instead of physically minor ones, sending valid dots to the loop emitter.
   Solution: Check for physically minor batch dimensions.

display_title: [XLA:CPU] Run post-layout simplification before fusion

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU] Run post-layout simplification before fusion

`AlgebraicSimplifier` only visits non-fusion computations. Running it after
`CpuInstructionFusion` and `FusionWrapper` meant that bitcast-equivalent copies
and reshapes left by `LayoutAssignment` (for example around LAPACK custom calls)
were wrapped into loop fusions instead of becoming bitcasts. Move the
simplification pipeline before fusion and drop the second `FusionWrapper`, which
only existed to wrap elementwise ops created by the late simplification.

Running the simplifier before fusion exposed two latent bugs, fixed here:

*   `AlgebraicSimplifier`: the `bitcast(unary(bitcast(x)))` rewrite treated
    `kCopy` as a pure elementwise op and dropped the layout change it performs.
*   `ElementalIrEmitter`: a fused `kBitcast` that changes the element type
    forwarded the operand value without an LLVM bitcast.

Context: https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/33666

display_title: [XLA] Check element types for kConvert in FloatSupport::EffectiveOperandPrecisionIsOutputPrecision.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Check element types for kConvert in FloatSupport::EffectiveOperandPrecisionIsOutputPrecision.

Make `FloatSupport::EffectiveOperandPrecisionIsOutputPrecision` a `const` member method and restrict `HloOpcode::kConvert` to same-type converts or transitions between `low_precision_type_` and `high_precision_type_`. Previously `kConvert` unconditionally returned `true`, which treated narrowing or unrelated converts (such as `F32 -> S32` or `F32 -> F16` under `BF16`/`F32` propagation) as preserving operand precision.

Same-type `kConvert` (`in_type == out_type`) is explicitly allowed because `BFloat16Propagation::RunImpl` inserts temporary `F32 -> F32` `kConvert` copies on `kWhile` inputs before running dataflow analysis to break buffer aliasing with external users. During the forward and backward propagation passes, proposed `BF16` demotions are recorded in `changes_to_bf16_` while the HLO instructions themselves remain `F32 -> F32` in the module until `MaterializeResolvedPrecisions` and `SkipNoopConversions` run at the end of the pass, so `AllUsersConsumeBF16` and `AddEdgesForUse` require `EffectiveOperandPrecisionIsOutputPrecision` to return `true` on those same-type converts.

head_commit.message:
PR #51216: Reclaim unused regions in growing PJRT GPU memory pools

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51216

## 📝 Summary of Changes

Enable BFC's existing whole-free-region reclamation for PJRT GPU pools when `preallocate=false`, honoring `TF_ENABLE_GPU_GARBAGE_COLLECTION` with a default of `true`. Preallocated pools keep their reservation behavior. Gate the allocator test dependency behind `if_google` because OSS `xla_cc_test` adds it automatically.

## 🎯 Justification

Growing pools can retain separate, wholly free backing regions that cannot satisfy a larger request. When the remaining growth allowance is too small, allocation fails even though reclaiming those regions would permit the request within the configured cap. This affected Gemma2-9B and Gemma3-4B training.

The fix enables the existing reclaim-and-retry path without moving live allocations or raising the cap. The environment override makes the opt-out advertised by BFC's reclamation warning effective for PJRT pools. It does not address true capacity exhaustion or fragmentation within regions containing live allocations.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix · 🧪 Tests

## 📊 Benchmark

No performance improvement claim; earlier workload validation checked successful execution and finite losses.

## 🧪 Unit Tests

- Eight GPU-independent cases cover reclamation with the setting unset/enabled/disabled, live-allocation and capacity preservation, preallocated-pool retention, and invalid settings; existing upstream sizing tests are preserved.
- The earlier revision passed 59 allocator tests and failed the reclamation regression without the fix. This rebased revision passes formatting, whitespace, and static dependency checks; compilation and tests were not rerun because compute resources were unavailable.

## 🧪 Execution Tests

- Earlier manual four-GPU Gemma2-9B and Gemma3-4B training runs each completed 101 steps with finite losses, with recomputation enabled and disabled; these were not rerun for this revision. No automated execution tests were added.
- Both modes used the same earlier runtime with the fix applied, without a separate pre-fix baseline; the Gemma2 enabled run exercised profiling but did not accept the recomputation rewrite.

display_title: Deprecate `tsl::strings::LegacyPrecision` in favor of `absl::HighPrecision`.

head_commit.message:
Deprecate `tsl::strings::LegacyPrecision` in favor of `absl::HighPrecision`.

`LegacyPrecision(float)` and `LegacyPrecision(double)` now forward to
`absl::HighPrecision`, and the custom `FpToBuffer` implementation is removed.

This is a value-preserving but not byte-identical change in formatting:
- float: the old implementation used %.6g and fell back to %.9g. absl uses
  the shortest of 6-9 significant digits that round-trips, e.g.
  1.17549435e-38f is now printed as "1.1754944e-38". This matches what the
  header comment already documented (%.6g, %.7g, %.8g, or %.9g).
- double: unchanged (%.15g, falling back to %.17g).
- NaN with the sign bit set is now printed as "nan" instead of "-nan".

All outputs still round-trip to the exact same value.

name: CI
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Visit all dots in GemmFusion instead of relying on a DFS.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Visit all dots in GemmFusion instead of relying on a DFS.

GemmFusion used a `DfsHloRewriteVisitor` driven by `computation->Accept()`.
`HandleDot` replaces instructions below the dot it is visiting (its epilogue)
and removes their now-unused operands. If one of those operands is still
pending on the DFS stack (e.g. `bitcast(other_dot)` as the other operand of a
fused multiply), it is removed before being expanded, so `other_dot` becomes
unreachable and is never visited. It then stays a plain dot and is later
rewritten to cuBLAS.

Collect the dots up front to make sure we visit each one.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1004034635

display_title: Synchronize external reference count tracking in the PJRT C API.

head_commit.message:
Synchronize external reference count tracking in the PJRT C API.

Concurrent calls to `PJRT_Buffer_IncreaseExternalReferenceCount` and `PJRT_Buffer_DecreaseExternalReferenceCount` race on `PJRT_Buffer::external_references`, which is an unsynchronized `std::vector`. Under concurrent host transfers or multi-threaded buffer access, unsynchronized `push_back` and `pop_back` calls corrupt the vector and can cause premature reference count underflow or crashes.

Guard `PJRT_Buffer::external_references` with the existing `PJRT_Buffer::mu` mutex in `xla/pjrt/c/pjrt_c_api_wrapper_impl.h`.

Add multi-threaded unit tests in `xla/pjrt/c/pjrt_c_api_test.cc` and `xla/pjrt/c_api_client/pjrt_c_api_client_test.cc` that exercise concurrent external reference acquisition and release, and verify that the net reference count returns to zero.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1001719588

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Keep the physical layout of the dot result in SplitkRewriter.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Keep the physical layout of the dot result in SplitkRewriter.

`SplitkRewriter` created the split-K dot with the default layout, regardless of the layout of the original dot result, and then forced the layout of the original dot result onto the split-K reduction. Whenever layout assignment had given the dot a non-default result layout (for example, `bf16[1536,256]{0,1}` for a dot whose result is transposed before it is consumed), the split-K reduction therefore also had to transpose its operand (`f32[8,1536,256]{2,1,0}` to `f32[1536,256]{0,1}`), which turns the cheap split-K reduction into a poorly coalesced transposing reduction.

Give the split-K dot the physical layout of the original dot result with the split-K dimension as the most major dimension instead, so that the reduction over the split-K dimension only sums contiguous slices of its operand. Triton emits the GEMM tiles in the requested layout at no extra cost. The result is numerically identical.

Add an end-to-end test that merges two quantized projections of the same activations (q and kv projections of an attention block), splits K, and checks that all split-K reductions read and write their operands in the default layout.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1003885965

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Swap GEMM operands when both generate code and RHS is larger.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Swap GEMM operands when both generate code and RHS is larger.

Previously, `GemmFusionSwapOperands` only swapped GEMM operands when:
1. Only the RHS producer generated non-trivial code and the LHS had a small non-contracting dimension (`< 128`), or
2. Neither operand generated code and the LHS had a smaller non-contracting dimension than the RHS (with LHS `< 128`).

When both the LHS and RHS producers of a dot in a Triton GEMM fusion generated code—for example, when the LHS has an activation/scale prologue (`convert` + `broadcast` + `multiply`) with a smaller non-contracting dimension (`M`) and the RHS has a weight dequantization prologue (`convert`) with a much larger non-contracting dimension (`N`)—`MaybeSwapOperands` returned early without swapping. Keeping the larger dimension on the RHS (`N`) prevented Triton from selecting tile shapes with a larger LHS tile and smaller RHS tile, causing autotuning to fall back to `CUBLASLT_FISSION` (unnesting the weight conversion into a separate memory-bound kernel that materializes the converted weights to global memory).

Update `MaybeSwapOperands` in `xla/backends/gpu/transforms/gemm_fusion_swap_operands.cc` so that when both operands generate code, we compare their non-contracting dimensions directly and swap them whenever the LHS non-contracting dimension is strictly smaller than the RHS non-contracting dimension (`lhs_noncontracting_size < rhs_noncontracting_size`). Add unit tests in `xla/backends/gpu/transforms/gemm_fusion_swap_operands_test.cc` covering both-code-generating, single-code-generating, and neither-code-generating cases.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1003355666

display_title: PR #50139: [ROCm] Export both SMI backend sources

head_commit.message:
PR #50139: [ROCm] Export both SMI backend sources

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50139

📝 Summary of Changes
This only changes a BUILD file. The exports are private.

🎯 Justification
This fixes `clang-tidy-cuda` on any PR that touches `smi_util_amd_smi.cc`:
```bash
  ERROR: no such target '//xla/stream_executor/rocm:smi_util_amd_smi.cc': target
  'smi_util_amd_smi.cc' not declared in package 'xla/stream_executor/rocm'
```
`run_clang_tidy.sh` passes the changed files as labels to `bazel cquery rdeps(...)`, and Bazel fails the whole query if any label is undeclared. The file is only in srcs when ROCm is 7.13 or newer. The CUDA config has no ROCm, so the file has no label. With the export, the query resolves.

🚀 Kind of Contribution: 🐛 Bug Fix

display_title: [ROCm] [CUDA] SKIP_PROFILED: allocate temp buffers in the VA reservation from the first execution PR 2/2

head_commit.message:
[ROCm] SKIP_PROFILED: allocate temp buffers in the VA reservation from the first execution

- In SKIP_PROFILED, automatically selected preallocated temp buffers are
  allocated at their VA reservation offsets from the first execution, as
  in SKIP_TEMP. A reservation created while profiling lays out every
  profile candidate (VA only); one created after the transition covers
  only the selected set.
- Before, the profiling executions took the temp from the regular VMM pool
  and the transition allocated a second copy in the reservation. The first
  copy stayed behind as stale allocator state, so each temp was held twice.
  On ROCm every peer imports each VMM mapping into its GTT, so the second
  copy overflowed GTT and multi-GPU runs hung; on CUDA it held extra device
  memory.
- Update the SKIP_PROFILED documentation in xla.proto and the class.
- Add unit tests for a reclaim-exempt temp under a one-temp PA budget, a
  shared profiling-phase reservation and a failed profiling execution;
  extend an existing test to the first execution.

name: CI
display_title: [ROCm] [CUDA] Release reservation-backed temp buffers when a VA-remapped execution fails before running PR 1/2

head_commit.message:
[ROCm] Release reservation-backed temp buffers when a VA-remapped execution fails before running

- GpuExecutable and the PJRT GPU client return without TearDown when
  setup before execution fails. With command buffer VA remapping
  (SKIP_TEMP, and SKIP_PROFILED after its transition) the temp buffer
  stayed active at its reservation address, so every later execution
  failed with ALREADY_EXISTS.
- Teardown now goes through ExecutionScope::TearDown in both callers. The
  VA-remap scope records the temps it allocates in the reservation and
  releases them in its destructor unless the scope was torn down.
- ExecutionScope stores the device ordinal it is created for; its methods
  no longer take one.
- Add unit tests for a failed allocation, an execution without teardown,
  and a teardown before an early return.

display_title: [ROCm] [CUDA] Serve pinned_host buffers from host memory with the VMM allocator PR 3/3

head_commit.message:
[ROCm] Serve pinned_host buffers from host memory with the VMM allocator

With the VMM allocator, pinned_host buffers got device memory with no
CPU mapping, so any CPU access segfaulted (orbax checkpoint saves, for
example). Command buffer update modes other than ALWAYS_UPDATE force
the VMM allocator, so they were affected too.

The PJRT GPU client now passes the VMM allocator the same pinned host
allocators the BFC path uses, through the generic
DeviceAddressVmmAllocator::Create() with no CUDA/ROCm #if branches.
Without a host allocator, MemorySpace::kHost now fails with
FailedPrecondition.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Visit all dots in GemmFusion instead of relying on a DFS.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Visit all dots in GemmFusion instead of relying on a DFS.

GemmFusion used a `DfsHloRewriteVisitor` driven by `computation->Accept()`.
`HandleDot` replaces instructions below the dot it is visiting (its epilogue)
and removes their now-unused operands. If one of those operands is still
pending on the DFS stack (e.g. `bitcast(other_dot)` as the other operand of a
fused multiply), it is removed before being expanded, so `other_dot` becomes
unreachable and is never visited. It then stays a plain dot and is later
rewritten to cuBLAS.

Collect the dots up front to make sure we visit each one.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1003275534

display_title: Support `UnpinnedHostMemorySpace` in PJRT GPU.

head_commit.message:
Support `UnpinnedHostMemorySpace` in PJRT GPU.

PJRT GPU devices previously only attached device HBM and pinned host memory spaces, preventing callers from allocating, importing, or transferring buffers in `UnpinnedHostMemorySpace`.

Attach `UnpinnedHostMemorySpace` to each addressable GPU device and register `UnpinnedHostMemorySpace::kKindId` in `StreamExecutorGpuTopologyDescription`. In `PjRtStreamExecutorRawClient`, delegate buffer allocation, foreign memory import, and event creation for `UnpinnedHostMemorySpace` to `CpuRawBuffer` and `CpuEvent`, and enable zero-copy host buffer import on GPU for unpinned host memory. Update `PjRtStreamExecutorRawBuffer` copy paths to route transfers targeting `UnpinnedHostMemorySpace` through host memory copies rather than intra-client StreamExecutor device transfers.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Reduce lock, cache-lookup, and thread-pool overhead in PriorityFusion.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Reduce lock, cache-lookup, and thread-pool overhead in PriorityFusion.

`CombinedGpuPerformanceModel` wrapped an already thread-safe `GpuPerformanceModelCache` with a redundant `cache_mutex_` and queried the cache before delegating to `GpuPerformanceModel::EstimateRunTimeForInstruction`, acquiring 6 mutex locks per instruction on a cache miss and 2 on a hit. Remove `cache_mutex_` and delegate non-Triton instructions directly to `GpuPerformanceModel::EstimateRunTimeForInstruction`.

In `PriorityFusionQueue`, check O(1) Triton eligibility flags before `ContainsScan` in `CanFuseTritonAsync`, use `can_fuse_cache_.find(producer)` instead of `operator[]` on cache lookup in `CanFuseCachedAsync`, and run single-instruction `ComputePriorities` inline on the calling thread instead of scheduling a thread-pool task with an `absl::BlockingCounter`.

display_title: [XLA] Memory-cost-aware latency hiding scheduler (kMemoryCost, aging, priced overlap)

head_commit.message:
[XLA] LHS: restrict kMemoryCost to pure releasers and rank it below async depth

Measured on model HLOs, the first version of kMemoryCost increased peak
memory: 93% of its decisions compared candidates that both *open* memory
(or an opener against a neutral op). For openers the bytes-per-time score
is backwards (it prefers slow openers over fast ones) and any neutral op
outranked any opener, so small consumers of large buffers (e.g. per-layer
amax reductions over saved activations) were hoisted out of their layer in
bottom-up order while their big-operand parents sank until the ready set
drained, then landed in one cluster far from the producers. Placing the
rule above kAsyncDepth also let it override the depth ordering that keeps
collectives overlapped.

Now a candidate only gets a score if it frees >= memory_aware_min_bytes
while opening < memory_aware_min_bytes; the policy returns no opinion
unless at least one candidate is such a releaser; and the rule is
evaluated after kAsyncDepth/kAvoidWaste so it only reorders within the
neighborhood the depth ordering already selected. Tests updated: openers
are no longer deferred (diamond), and a net releaser that opens a large
buffer is neutral.

display_title: [XLA] Check element types for kConvert in FloatSupport::EffectiveOperandPrecisionIsOutputPrecision.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Check element types for kConvert in FloatSupport::EffectiveOperandPrecisionIsOutputPrecision.

Make `FloatSupport::EffectiveOperandPrecisionIsOutputPrecision` a `const` member method and restrict `HloOpcode::kConvert` to same-type converts or transitions between `low_precision_type_` and `high_precision_type_`. Previously `kConvert` unconditionally returned `true`, which treated narrowing or unrelated converts (such as `F32 -> S32` or `F32 -> F16` under `BF16`/`F32` propagation) as preserving operand precision.

Same-type `kConvert` (`in_type == out_type`) is explicitly allowed because `BFloat16Propagation::RunImpl` inserts temporary `F32 -> F32` `kConvert` copies on `kWhile` inputs before running dataflow analysis to break buffer aliasing with external users. During the forward and backward propagation passes, proposed `BF16` demotions are recorded in `changes_to_bf16_` while the HLO instructions themselves remain `F32 -> F32` in the module until `MaterializeResolvedPrecisions` and `SkipNoopConversions` run at the end of the pass, so `AllUsersConsumeBF16` and `AddEdgesForUse` require `EffectiveOperandPrecisionIsOutputPrecision` to return `true` on those same-type converts.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1003317196

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Fold per-channel dot output scales into the dequantized dot operand.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Fold per-channel dot output scales into the dequantized dot operand.

Weight-only quantized matmuls are often expressed as
`multiply(dot(x, convert(w)), broadcast(scale))`, with the per-output-channel
dequantization scale applied to the result of the dot. On GPU the dot is
emitted as a Triton GEMM fusion that already dequantizes `w` in its
prologue, while the scale multiply ends up in a separate kernel after the
GEMM (and, for split-K GEMMs, after the split-K reduction), where it also
prevents other consumers of the GEMM from fusing with it.

Add a rewrite to GpuAlgebraicSimplifier that folds the scale into the
dequantized operand instead,
`dot(x, multiply(convert(w), broadcast(scale)))`, when the scale only varies
along batch and non-contracting dimensions of the dequantized operand. The
multiply then fuses into the GEMM prologue next to the convert. Single-user
transposes and reshapes between the dot and the multiply (e.g. the transpose
JAX inserts for `bsd,ckdh->cbskh` einsums) and between the convert and the
dot are looked through, and degenerate scale dimensions are dropped. The
rewrite also applies before DotMerger merges dots that share the activation
operand; GEMM fusion fuses the scaled operands through the resulting
concatenate.

Applying the scale to the dequantized weights instead of to the accumulated
result changes rounding, so the rewrite is behind the new flag
`--xla_gpu_experimental_enable_dot_output_scale_folding` (off by default).

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1003885964

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Keep the physical layout of the dot result in SplitkRewriter.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Keep the physical layout of the dot result in SplitkRewriter.

SplitkRewriter created the split-K dot with the default layout, regardless
of the layout of the original dot result, and then forced the layout of the
original dot result onto the split-K reduction. Whenever layout assignment
had given the dot a non-default result layout (e.g. `bf16[1536,256]{0,1}`
for a dot whose result is transposed before it is consumed), the split-K
reduction therefore also had to transpose its operand
(`f32[8,1536,256]{2,1,0} -> f32[1536,256]{0,1}`), which turns the cheap
split-K reduction into a poorly coalesced transposing reduction.

Give the split-K dot the physical layout of the original dot result with the
split-K dimension as the most major dimension instead, so that the
reduction over the split-K dimension only sums contiguous slices of its
operand. Triton emits the GEMM tiles in the requested layout at no extra
cost. The result is numerically identical.

Adds an end-to-end test that merges two quantized projections of the same
activations (q and kv projections of an attention block), splits K and
checks that all split-K reductions read and write their operands in the
default layout.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1003885965

name: CI
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Add producer fencing to SchedulerMemoryFencing

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Anchor producer fences to large-buffer releases

Anchoring producers to async windows does not pin them: the latency-hiding
scheduler moves async starts freely (on Gemma2-27B it hoisted the anchoring
all-gather-start by ~470 positions and the fenced GEMMs with it), so the
fence recovered only part of the peak-memory regression.

Instead, fence each (non-async) producer of a large buffer to the last use of
the (producer_slack + 1)-th most recent large buffer released before it in the
reference schedule. This keeps the relative order of large allocation and
release events close to the memory-minimizing reference schedule, which is
what bounds their simultaneous liveness, while leaving async starts and small
ops free. Buffers defined by async operations never receive a producer edge
so collective overlap stays unconstrained. The flag is renamed to
--xla_gpu_experimental_scheduler_memory_fencing_producer_slack.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Cache ContainsSignificantReduce and fast-path non-fusions in FusionInfoCache.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Cache ContainsSignificantReduce and fast-path non-fusions in FusionInfoCache.

In `PriorityFusionQueue::CanFuseWithNativeEmitter`, checking whether a producer or consumer contains a significant reduction (reduction factor >= 16) previously allocated an `HloFusionAdaptor` and traversed all instructions in the fusion on every `(producer, consumer)` pair without caching.

Move this check to `ContainsSignificantReduce` in `gpu_fusible` and cache the result for fusion instructions in `FusionInfoCache` (mirroring `ContainsScan`), guarding against zero-extent reduction output shapes before dividing. Also consolidate `FusionInfoCache` lookups into a shared `GetOrCompute` helper that evaluates non-fusion instructions (`instr.opcode() != HloOpcode::kFusion`) directly without acquiring `mutex_` or populating the cache maps, uses `absl::ReaderMutexLock` for concurrent fusion cache hits, acquires `mutex_` in `Invalidate`, and annotates cache maps with `ABSL_GUARDED_BY(mutex_)`.

head_commit.message:
PR #51246: [ROCm] Skip the hipGraphGetNodes count in PrepareFinalization on update

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51246

## 📝 Summary of Changes

`RocmCommandBuffer::PrepareFinalization()` returns early when the command buffer is being updated, so `Finalize()`
after `Update()` no longer asks HIP for the graph's node count.

## 🎯 Justification

Every time XLA updates a ROCm command buffer, it asks HIP how many nodes the graph has, and it does this right before launching the graph. HIP has no cheap way to answer: it topologically sorts the whole graph just to return the count. The count can't change during an update, so the work is wasted, and it sits on the host's critical path before every updated `hipGraphLaunch`.

Only `Create*` methods add nodes, and they all require `State::kCreate`, so the create-time finalization has already
made the graph non-empty.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

⚡️ Performance Improvement · 🧪 Tests

## 🧪 Unit Tests

`GpuCommandBufferTest.UpdateEmptyCommandBuffer` (`xla/stream_executor/gpu/gpu_command_buffer_test.cc`): an empty
command buffer is finalized, submitted, updated, finalized and submitted again. It covers the ROCm path and is skipped
on CUDA.

head_commit.message:
PR #51246: [ROCm] Skip the hipGraphGetNodes count in PrepareFinalization on update

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51246

## 📝 Summary of Changes

`RocmCommandBuffer::PrepareFinalization()` returns early when the command buffer is being updated, so `Finalize()`
after `Update()` no longer asks HIP for the graph's node count.

## 🎯 Justification

Every time XLA updates a ROCm command buffer, it asks HIP how many nodes the graph has, and it does this right before launching the graph. HIP has no cheap way to answer: it topologically sorts the whole graph just to return the count. The count can't change during an update, so the work is wasted, and it sits on the host's critical path before every updated `hipGraphLaunch`.

Only `Create*` methods add nodes, and they all require `State::kCreate`, so the create-time finalization has already
made the graph non-empty.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

⚡️ Performance Improvement · 🧪 Tests

## 🧪 Unit Tests

`GpuCommandBufferTest.UpdateEmptyCommandBuffer` (`xla/stream_executor/gpu/gpu_command_buffer_test.cc`): an empty
command buffer is finalized, submitted, updated, finalized and submitted again. It covers the ROCm path and is skipped
on CUDA.

display_title: [XLA] Speed up HloEvaluator::HandleReduce for integer, tuple, and large-output reductions.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Speed up HloEvaluator::HandleReduce for integer, tuple, and large-output reductions.

Previously, `HloEvaluator::HandleReduce` used a fast path only for single-output floating-point scalar `kAdd` reductions. For integer reductions and variadic tuple reductions, `GenerateReduceOutputElement` ran an embedded `HloEvaluator` on every input element. Each reduction step allocated and destroyed scalar `Literal` objects and called `DecomposeTuple()`. In addition, for every output element, `GenerateReduceOutputElement` and `ShapeUtil::ForEachIndexNoStatus` allocated temporary index `std::vector` objects on the heap. On large reductions across many worker threads, these heap allocations caused high allocator lock contention and 900s test timeouts.

Extend `MatchSimpleBinaryReducer` to match single-output and variadic tuple reductions over simple scalar binary operations (`kAdd`, `kMultiply`, `kMaximum`, `kMinimum`, `kAnd`, `kOr`, `kXor`). Keep chunked `double` accumulation (`GetSumAsDouble`) for floating-point `kAdd` reductions. Evaluate all other matched binary reductions in native types over raw input buffers without heap allocations, and skip creating per-thread `embedded_evaluators`. Precompute linear strides per input argument (`SimpleReducePlan`) to iterate over reduced dimensions without per-output-element heap allocations or multidimensional index conversions. For general reductions that use the embedded evaluator, allocate `arg_values`, `accumulators`, and `embedded_operands` once per output element, and read tuple outputs with `LiteralSlice` instead of `DecomposeTuple()`.

Misc:

- Unify single-output and variadic tuple reduction matching in `MatchSimpleBinaryReducers` and remove the separate `IsScalarAdd` helper.
- Extract `SimpleReduceElementwiseType` to deduplicate the elementwise type alias across `EvaluateSimpleReduceElement` and `EvaluateSimpleReduceWindowTyped`.
- Coalesce contiguous reduced dimensions in `MakeSimpleReducePlan` and remove the unreachable zero-count branch after `ShapeUtil::IsZeroElementArray`.
- Separate the fast-path and slow-path parallel loops in `HloEvaluator::HandleReduce`, standardize `arg_dim_counts` / `arg_dim_steps` parameter order in `GenerateReduceOutputElement`, and use `DimensionVector` for dimension metadata.
- Add unit tests in `hlo_evaluator_test.cc` covering contiguous 2D, non-contiguous 2D/3D, trivial-dimension, zero-element, non-default-layout, and commuted-operand reductions.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1003835549

display_title: [XLA] Check element types for kConvert in FloatSupport::EffectiveOperandPrecisionIsOutputPrecision.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Check element types for kConvert in FloatSupport::EffectiveOperandPrecisionIsOutputPrecision.

Make `FloatSupport::EffectiveOperandPrecisionIsOutputPrecision` a `const` member method and restrict `HloOpcode::kConvert` to same-type converts or transitions between `low_precision_type_` and `high_precision_type_`. Previously `kConvert` unconditionally returned `true`, which treated narrowing or unrelated converts (such as `F32 -> S32` or `F32 -> F16` under `BF16`/`F32` propagation) as preserving operand precision.

Same-type `kConvert` (`in_type == out_type`) is explicitly allowed because `BFloat16Propagation::RunImpl` inserts temporary `F32 -> F32` `kConvert` copies on `kWhile` inputs before running dataflow analysis to break buffer aliasing with external users. During the forward and backward propagation passes, proposed `BF16` demotions are recorded in `changes_to_bf16_` while the HLO instructions themselves remain `F32 -> F32` in the module until `MaterializeResolvedPrecisions` and `SkipNoopConversions` run at the end of the pass, so `AllUsersConsumeBF16` and `AddEdgesForUse` require `EffectiveOperandPrecisionIsOutputPrecision` to return `true` on those same-type converts.

name: CI
display_title: Avoid redundant analysis and RBE downloads in CI

head_commit.message:
Avoid redundant analysis and RBE downloads in CI

In `build_tools/ci/build.py` we used to run a separate `bazel build --nobuild` step before the actual `bazel build` or `bazel test` invocation to retry repository fetches. This added a second target-analysis pass (~5-30s on most builds, and ~2.5 min on `Hermetic ROCm` where `+rocm_configure_ext` re-evaluated the main repo mapping) plus BES upload overhead.

Instead let's configure `--experimental_repository_downloader_retries=5` in `tensorflow.bazelrc` so Bazel retries transient download errors in-process without a second invocation, and remove `bazel build --nobuild` from `build_tools/ci/build.py`.

Also:

1. Switch `common:rbe_base` in `tensorflow.bazelrc` (and the Linux JAX RBE builds in `build_tools/ci/build.py`) to `--remote_download_minimal` and `--nobuild_runfile_links` so CI shards still compile and link all non-test binaries on RBE without downloading them or materializing runfiles symlink trees when they are not executed locally.
2. Keep `--remote_download_toplevel` and `--build_runfile_links` enabled for the benchmark presubmit builds (which execute the built binaries from `bazel-bin`) and `--remote_download_toplevel` for `clang-tidy-common` (which reads the generated `.clang-tidy.yaml` files from disk).

Comparing full builds with a warm RBE cache (https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50787 vs. https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51241), this reduces `Run build.py` times across RBE jobs:

- `XLA Linux x86 GPU Hermetic ROCm` (always full build): 11m 49s -> 6m 08s (-2m 38s from removing `--nobuild`, -2m 59s in execution/download phase)
- `XLA Linux X86 GPU ONEAPI` (always full build): 4m 36s -> 3m 49s (-43s in execution/download phase)
- `JAX Linux x86 GPU T4` (always full build): 2m 27s -> 2m 09s (-16s in execution/download phase)
- `XLA Linux x86 CPU WORKSPACE` (full build, warm RBE cache): 7m 54s -> 2m 22s (execution/download phase drops from 6m 27s to 59s; 3,811 fewer `.runfiles` actions)
- `XLA Linux x86 GPU T4` (full build, warm RBE cache): 7m 53s -> 3m 41s (execution/download phase drops from 5m 35s to 1m 08s; 3,029 fewer `.runfiles` actions)

display_title: PR #48089: [XLA:GPU] Fix loop emitter insert point after emitting a loop mid-block

head_commit.message:
PR #48089: [XLA:GPU] Fix loop emitter insert point after emitting a loop mid-block

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/48089

## 📝 Summary of Changes

Fixes #47372.

A sort comparator that computes non-scalar intermediate values crashes GPU
compilation with `llvm_loop.cc:76] Check failed:
!preheader_bb_->hasTerminator()`. The GPU nested computation emitter
(`CodegenNestedComputation`) emits comparators as inline functions with the
builder positioned before a pre-created `ret void`. The first multi-element
op emits its loop through `ForLoop::Emit`'s split path, which moves the
`ret` into the new `loop_exit` block. `LoopEmitter::EmitLoop` (and
`ForLoop::Emit` itself) then reposition the builder at the end of
`loop_exit`, which is after the moved `ret`. The next loop-emitting op sees
an insert point at the end of a terminated block and trips the CHECK.

The fix repositions the builder at the exit block's first insertion point
instead of its end, in both `LoopEmitter::EmitLoop` and `ForLoop::Emit`.
For the common case (the loop was emitted at the end of an unterminated
block, so the exit block is a fresh empty block) this is identical to the
old behavior. For the mid-block split case it puts follow-up code where the
original insertion point was: before whatever the split moved into the exit
block. `ParallelLoopEmitter::EmitLoop` already handles its exit block this
way; the shared llvm_ir helpers never did.

## 🎯 Justification

The module in the issue is valid HLO (plain ops, runs fine on CPU and
interpreter); the GPU backend aborts the whole process while compiling it.
Any custom sort comparator with non-scalar intermediates that survive
simplification hits this, as does any nested call computation emitted
through `CallNestedComputation`. The crash reproduces without any XLA
flags.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

## 🧪 Unit Tests:

`SortTest.MultiElementComparator` in `xla/tests/sort_test.cc`: sorts
`f32[32]` with a comparator that is semantically `p0 < p1` but computed
through `f32[2]` intermediates (iota, two broadcasts, two adds, elementwise
compare, slice, reshape), compared against the interpreter reference with
zero tolerance. Without the fix the GPU test dies on the `llvm_loop.cc:76`
CHECK; with the fix it passes. `sort_test_cpu`, `sort_test_nvgpu_any`, all
`//xla/service/llvm_ir/...` and `//xla/service/cpu/tests/...` targets pass
with the change.

## 🧪 Execution Tests:

The issue's original StableHLO module and a reduced 19-line HLO module both
compile and run on one GPU (RTX 2070, sm_75) with the fix and abort at the
CHECK without it. The fixed binary's outputs match the interpreter
elementwise for order-consistent comparators.
Copybara import of the project:

--
2b030bf33c80fbf195afa04ddbe31f0a17eb24b1 by Stanislav Bardyuk <sbardyuk@google.com>:

[XLA:GPU] Fix loop emitter insert point after emitting a loop mid-block

ForLoop::Emit supports emitting a loop in the middle of a basic block by
splitting it; splitBasicBlock moves the tail of the block, including its
terminator, into the new loop_exit block. But after emitting the loop,
ForLoop::Emit and LoopEmitter::EmitLoop repositioned the builder at the
end of loop_exit, i.e. after the moved terminator. The GPU nested
computation emitter hits exactly this: it emits sort comparators inline
with the builder parked before a pre-created ret. A comparator with two
or more non-scalar intermediate values then crashes on the
llvm_loop.cc:76 CHECK when the second loop is emitted at the end of the
already-terminated loop_exit block.

Reposition the builder at the exit block's first insertion point
instead, which is where the pre-split insertion point's continuation
belongs. For loops emitted at the end of an unterminated block the exit
block is empty and this is identical to the previous behavior.
ParallelLoopEmitter::EmitLoop already handles its exit block this way.

Fixes #47372.

Merging this change closes #48089

head_commit.message:
PR #48089: [XLA:GPU] Fix loop emitter insert point after emitting a loop mid-block

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/48089

## 📝 Summary of Changes

Fixes #47372.

A sort comparator that computes non-scalar intermediate values crashes GPU
compilation with `llvm_loop.cc:76] Check failed:
!preheader_bb_->hasTerminator()`. The GPU nested computation emitter
(`CodegenNestedComputation`) emits comparators as inline functions with the
builder positioned before a pre-created `ret void`. The first multi-element
op emits its loop through `ForLoop::Emit`'s split path, which moves the
`ret` into the new `loop_exit` block. `LoopEmitter::EmitLoop` (and
`ForLoop::Emit` itself) then reposition the builder at the end of
`loop_exit`, which is after the moved `ret`. The next loop-emitting op sees
an insert point at the end of a terminated block and trips the CHECK.

The fix repositions the builder at the exit block's first insertion point
instead of its end, in both `LoopEmitter::EmitLoop` and `ForLoop::Emit`.
For the common case (the loop was emitted at the end of an unterminated
block, so the exit block is a fresh empty block) this is identical to the
old behavior. For the mid-block split case it puts follow-up code where the
original insertion point was: before whatever the split moved into the exit
block. `ParallelLoopEmitter::EmitLoop` already handles its exit block this
way; the shared llvm_ir helpers never did.

## 🎯 Justification

The module in the issue is valid HLO (plain ops, runs fine on CPU and
interpreter); the GPU backend aborts the whole process while compiling it.
Any custom sort comparator with non-scalar intermediates that survive
simplification hits this, as does any nested call computation emitted
through `CallNestedComputation`. The crash reproduces without any XLA
flags.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

## 🧪 Unit Tests:

`SortTest.MultiElementComparator` in `xla/tests/sort_test.cc`: sorts
`f32[32]` with a comparator that is semantically `p0 < p1` but computed
through `f32[2]` intermediates (iota, two broadcasts, two adds, elementwise
compare, slice, reshape), compared against the interpreter reference with
zero tolerance. Without the fix the GPU test dies on the `llvm_loop.cc:76`
CHECK; with the fix it passes. `sort_test_cpu`, `sort_test_nvgpu_any`, all
`//xla/service/llvm_ir/...` and `//xla/service/cpu/tests/...` targets pass
with the change.

## 🧪 Execution Tests:

The issue's original StableHLO module and a reduced 19-line HLO module both
compile and run on one GPU (RTX 2070, sm_75) with the fix and abort at the
CHECK without it. The fixed binary's outputs match the interpreter
elementwise for order-consistent comparators.
Copybara import of the project:

--
2b030bf33c80fbf195afa04ddbe31f0a17eb24b1 by Stanislav Bardyuk <sbardyuk@google.com>:

[XLA:GPU] Fix loop emitter insert point after emitting a loop mid-block

ForLoop::Emit supports emitting a loop in the middle of a basic block by
splitting it; splitBasicBlock moves the tail of the block, including its
terminator, into the new loop_exit block. But after emitting the loop,
ForLoop::Emit and LoopEmitter::EmitLoop repositioned the builder at the
end of loop_exit, i.e. after the moved terminator. The GPU nested
computation emitter hits exactly this: it emits sort comparators inline
with the builder parked before a pre-created ret. A comparator with two
or more non-scalar intermediate values then crashes on the
llvm_loop.cc:76 CHECK when the second loop is emitted at the end of the
already-terminated loop_exit block.

Reposition the builder at the exit block's first insertion point
instead, which is where the pre-split insertion point's continuation
belongs. For loops emitted at the end of an unterminated block the exit
block is empty and this is identical to the previous behavior.
ParallelLoopEmitter::EmitLoop already handles its exit block this way.

Fixes #47372.

Merging this change closes #48089

display_title: PR #51246: [ROCm] Skip the hipGraphGetNodes count in PrepareFinalization on update

head_commit.message:
PR #51246: [ROCm] Skip the hipGraphGetNodes count in PrepareFinalization on update

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51246

## 📝 Summary of Changes

`RocmCommandBuffer::PrepareFinalization()` returns early when the command buffer is being updated, so `Finalize()`
after `Update()` no longer asks HIP for the graph's node count.

## 🎯 Justification

Every time XLA updates a ROCm command buffer, it asks HIP how many nodes the graph has, and it does this right before launching the graph. HIP has no cheap way to answer: it topologically sorts the whole graph just to return the count. The count can't change during an update, so the work is wasted, and it sits on the host's critical path before every updated `hipGraphLaunch`.

Only `Create*` methods add nodes, and they all require `State::kCreate`, so the create-time finalization has already
made the graph non-empty.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

⚡️ Performance Improvement · 🧪 Tests

## 🧪 Unit Tests

`GpuCommandBufferTest.UpdateEmptyCommandBuffer` (`xla/stream_executor/gpu/gpu_command_buffer_test.cc`): an empty
command buffer is finalized, submitted, updated, finalized and submitted again. It covers the ROCm path and is skipped
on CUDA.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Defer CUDA VMM memory deallocations while a cuDNN handle is active.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Defer CUDA VMM memory deallocations while a cuDNN handle is active.

cuDNN v9 internally captures temporary CUDA graphs during heuristic queries and execution plan creation (e.g. via `cudnn::backend::cudnnBackendGetMetadataFromGraph` inside `cudnnBackendFinalize`), which does not go through `CudaStream::CaptureHandle`.

During parallel autotuning (`ConfigAssigner::GetConfigsForAll`), a worker thread running `GpuProfiler::Profile` can deallocate VMM buffers via `CudaDeviceMemoryAllocation::~CudaDeviceMemoryAllocation` -> `DrainPendingVmmDeallocations` -> `cuCtxSynchronize()` concurrently with the main thread querying cuDNN heuristics in `CudnnSupport::GetConvolveRunners`. Calling `cuCtxSynchronize()` while cuDNN is capturing a CUDA graph on the same CUDA context either fails with `CUDA_ERROR_STREAM_CAPTURE_UNSUPPORTED` / `cudaErrorStreamCaptureInvalidated` or segfaults inside `libcuda.so` (`cuCtxSynchronize`).

Call `CudaDeviceAllocator::EnterStreamCapture` and `CudaDeviceAllocator::ExitStreamCapture` in `CudnnHandle` (`xla/stream_executor/cuda/cuda_dnn.cc`) so that VMM deallocations are deferred until the active cuDNN operation completes.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1003883162

display_title: [XLA:BufferAssignment] Derive the OOM fallback chain from the algorithm.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:BufferAssignment] Derive the OOM fallback chain from the algorithm.

We have two flags: one enables fast buffer assignment with the fallback
(`--xla_tpu_buffer_assignment_enable_fast_merge_fallback`), and the other
specifies the buffer assignment algorithm (`--xla_tpu_buffer_assignment_algorithm`).

With the fallback enabled, the algorithm for AssignBuffersWithSequentialOrdering specified via `--xla_tpu_buffer_assignment_algorithm` now defines the fallback chain. Previously, enabling the fallback led to not respecting `--xla_tpu_buffer_assignment_algorithm`.

The pairs below are (non-sequential, sequential) algorithms. Depending on `--xla_tpu_buffer_assignment_algorithm`:

* auto, FAST_MERGE: (FAST_MERGE, FAST_MERGE) → (FAST_MERGE, FAST_SPLIT) → (DEFAULT, DEFAULT)
* FAST_SPLIT: (FAST_MERGE, FAST_SPLIT) → (DEFAULT, DEFAULT)
* TEMPORAL: (FAST_MERGE, TEMPORAL) → (DEFAULT, DEFAULT)
* SPATIAL: (FAST_MERGE, SPATIAL) → (DEFAULT, SPATIAL)
* DEFAULT (=SPATIAL): (FAST_MERGE, DEFAULT) → (DEFAULT, DEFAULT)
* BEST_OF_SPATIAL_TEMPORAL: (FAST_MERGE, BEST_OF_SPATIAL_TEMPORAL) → (DEFAULT, BEST_OF_SPATIAL_TEMPORAL)

If the fallback flag is disabled, we respect the specified algorithm, and
nothing changes.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Normalize dot batch dimensions only when cuBLAS cannot handle the layout.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Normalize dot batch dimensions only when cuBLAS cannot handle the layout.

1. Problem: cuBLAS natively supports multiple batch dimensions when physically
   sequential (which layout assignment ensures), yet GemmRewriter always
   collapsed them.
   Solution: Skip batch normalization when MatrixLayout accepts the layouts.

2. Problem: When normalization is needed (e.g. after SplitkRewriter),
   GemmRewriter only merged 2 batch dimensions and emitted reshapes that failed
   in the fission autotuner.
   Solution: Merge all batch dimensions into one, bitcasting when possible and
   transposing to default layout otherwise.

3. Problem: IsCublasSupportedMatMul rejected logically last batch dimensions
   instead of physically minor ones, sending valid dots to the loop emitter.
   Solution: Check for physically minor batch dimensions.

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50858

### :pencil: Summary of Changes

Make GPU topology `platform_version()` report the software version, such as `cuda 13040`, consistently with the GPU client. Share the existing version formatter and preserve GPU model names in `device_kind()` and serialized topology metadata. This addresses failure in JAX which depends on the topology `platform_version` reporting the CUDA version rather than device name.

The intent from the comments appears to be that `platform_version` from the compile client should be the CUDA version rather than the device name \[1\], but this isn't how it is actually populated \[2\]:

      // Returns a string containing human-readable, platform-specific version info

```

     if (gpu_topology.platform_version().empty()) {

```

PR #51324: Bump numpy from 2.4.6 to 2.5.4 Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51324 Bumps [numpy](https://github.com/numpy/numpy) from 2.4.6 to 2.5.4.
Release notes

Sourced from numpy's releases.

v2.5.4 (Oct 10, 2026)

NumPy 2.5.4 Release Notes

Released on 2026-10-10.

NumPy 2.5.4 is a patch release that fixes bugs discovered after the 2.5.3 release. Highlights are:

  • Many typing fixes and improvements,
  • A workaround for the MSVC 19.51 bug, see below.

This release supports Python versions 3.12-3.15.

Improvements

  • numpy.linalg.svd and numpy.linalg.lstsq now raise for inputs containing infinities instead of returning garbage results.

  • Fixed hangs in numpy.linalg.svd and numpy.linalg.lstsq for certain inputs containing infinities for recent versions of some LAPACK implementations.

  • numpy.linalg.cond now handles non-finite inputs more consistently.

(gh-32593)

StringDType hashing with NaN sentinels

StringDType instances with equivalent floating-point NaN sentinels now have equal hashes. Previously, distinct NaN objects could produce equal dtype instances with different hashes, causing dictionary lookups and set deduplication to fail.

(gh-32563)

Changes

MaskedArray resets a fill_value that cannot be represented in a new dtype

A fill_value copied from a source array is now reset to the default fill_value for the new dtype when it cannot be represented in that dtype. Previously the copied value could be stale: ufuncs that change dtype left the result holding a fill_value typed for the old dtype, which raised a TypeError only when something later validated it (such as .view()), and a floating point fill_value that overflows an integer dtype was kept as an out-of-range value together with a RuntimeWarning. Both now fall back to the default, including when a masked array is passed to MaskedArray with a different dtype. A fill_value given explicitly by the user is still validated and raises as before. This can now raise a ComplexWarning if the fill_value is complex and the new dtype is real.

PR #50858: [PJRT:GPU] Align topology and client platform versions

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50858

### :pencil: Summary of Changes

Make GPU topology `platform_version()` report the software version, such as `cuda 13040`, consistently with the GPU client. Share the existing version formatter and preserve GPU model names in `device_kind()` and serialized topology metadata. This addresses failure in JAX which depends on the topology `platform_version` reporting the CUDA version rather than device name.

The intent from the comments appears to be that `platform_version` from the compile client should be the CUDA version rather than the device name \[1\], but this isn't how it is actually populated \[2\]:

\[1\] https://github.com/openxla/xla/blob/main/xla/pjrt/pjrt_client.h#L614-L616

```
      // Returns a string containing human-readable, platform-specific version info
   // (e.g. the CUDA version on GPU or libtpu version on Cloud TPU).
   virtual absl::string_view platform_version() const = 0;
```

\[2\] https://github.com/openxla/xla/blob/main/xla/pjrt/distributed/topology_util.cc#L422-L424

```
     if (gpu_topology.platform_version().empty()) {
    gpu_topology.set_platform_version(device.name());
  }
```

GPU compile-only clients inherit their platform version from the topology, which previously returned the device model. This fixes inconsistent metadata between runtime and compile-only clients, benefiting JAX/XLA AOT and deviceless compilation workflows.

PR #48089: [XLA:GPU] Fix loop emitter insert point after emitting a loop mid-block

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/48089

## 📝 Summary of Changes

Fixes #47372.

A sort comparator that computes non-scalar intermediate values crashes GPU
compilation with `llvm_loop.cc:76] Check failed:
!preheader_bb_->hasTerminator()`. The GPU nested computation emitter
(`CodegenNestedComputation`) emits comparators as inline functions with the
builder positioned before a pre-created `ret void`. The first multi-element
op emits its loop through `ForLoop::Emit`'s split path, which moves the
`ret` into the new `loop_exit` block. `LoopEmitter::EmitLoop` (and
`ForLoop::Emit` itself) then reposition the builder at the end of
`loop_exit`, which is after the moved `ret`. The next loop-emitting op sees
an insert point at the end of a terminated block and trips the CHECK.

The fix repositions the builder at the exit block's first insertion point
instead of its end, in both `LoopEmitter::EmitLoop` and `ForLoop::Emit`.

original insertion point was: before whatever the split moved into the exit
block. `ParallelLoopEmitter::EmitLoop` already handles its exit block this
way; the shared llvm_ir helpers never did.

The module in the issue is valid HLO (plain ops, runs fine on CPU and
interpreter); the GPU backend aborts the whole process while compiling it.
Any custom sort comparator with non-scalar intermediates that survive
simplification hits this, as does any nested call computation emitted

display_title: PR #50225: [XLA:GPU] Support multi-output fusion in the concatenate emitter

head_commit.message:
PR #50225: [XLA:GPU] Support multi-output fusion in the concatenate emitter

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50225

📝 Summary of Changes
- The concatenate emitter emits fusions with several roots. Each distinct hero is computed once per operand loop, and one shared epilogue writes all outputs.
- UseConcatenateFusion accepts several roots when the heroes are concatenates with identical splits, the roots share one shape, and roots × operands ≤ 6. It rejects a non-elementwise op in the epilogue that reads a hero.
- The multi-output fusion pass merges concatenate fusions only if the result keeps the concatenate emitter.

🎯 Justification
Equal-shaped concatenates over the same inputs, as in the Eigh expander's Jacobi permutations, ran as separate kernels or fell back to the loop emitter. Now they run as one kernel that reads each operand once. This also merges RoPE q/k concatenate pairs in some models.

🚀 Kind of Contribution:  ⚡️ Performance Improvement,

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)
This Eigh example gets a ~20% improvement on MI350:

```bash
HloModule Test
ENTRY Random_1000 {
  a.1 = f32[1000,1000]{1,0} parameter(0)
  ROOT CC = (f32[1000,1000]{1,0}, f32[1000]{0}) custom-call(a.1), custom_call_target="Eigh", backend_config="1,1,15,0.000010"
}
```

On gpt_j_6b, the RoPE q/k pairs merge in every transformer layer, but the overall end-to-end performance change is negligible.

🧪 Unit Tests:
hlo_fusion_analysis_test.cc and multi_output_fusion_test.cc cover the accepted shapes, the operand budget, mismatched splits and shapes, hero reads through non-elementwise ops (including inside the second sibling), and a layer-norm producer reduced from AlphaFold 3. Two FileCheck tests in emitters/tests/concatenate/ cover shape-changing epilogues and a shared hero.

🧪 Execution Tests:
Both FileCheck tests also run gpu_test_correctness on one GPU.

PR #51162: [ROCm] Hide GCC 8 std::filesystem symbols.

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51162

📝 Summary of Changes
`mori_application` no longer exports the GCC 8 `std::filesystem` code it links statically from `libstdc++fs.a` (`-Wl,--exclude-libs,libstdc++fs.a`), or its inline `path` members (`-fvisibility-inlines-hidden`).

🎯 Justification
The hermetic toolchain's GCC 8 `std::filesystem` is ABI-incompatible with the system `libstdc++.so.6`. MORI's exported copy took over hipBLASLt's calls. This affects ROCm tests that load MORI and call into hipBLASLt or other ROCm libraries that use `std::filesystem`.

🚀 Kind of Contribution
Please remove what does not apply: 🐛 Bug Fix

🧪 Unit Tests:
//xla/backends/gpu/codegen/triton/tests:fusion_emitter_int4_device_test_amdgpu_any

Copybara import of the project:

name: CI
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Defer CUDA VMM memory deallocations while a cuDNN handle is active.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Defer CUDA VMM memory deallocations while a cuDNN handle is active.

cuDNN v9 internally captures temporary CUDA graphs during heuristic queries and execution plan creation (e.g. via `cudnn::backend::cudnnBackendGetMetadataFromGraph` inside `cudnnBackendFinalize`), which does not go through `CudaStream::CaptureHandle`.

During parallel autotuning (`ConfigAssigner::GetConfigsForAll`), a worker thread running `GpuProfiler::Profile` can deallocate VMM buffers via `CudaDeviceMemoryAllocation::~CudaDeviceMemoryAllocation` -> `DrainPendingVmmDeallocations` -> `cuCtxSynchronize()` concurrently with the main thread querying cuDNN heuristics in `CudnnSupport::GetConvolveRunners`. Calling `cuCtxSynchronize()` while cuDNN is capturing a CUDA graph on the same CUDA context either fails with `CUDA_ERROR_STREAM_CAPTURE_UNSUPPORTED` / `cudaErrorStreamCaptureInvalidated` or segfaults inside `libcuda.so` (`cuCtxSynchronize`).

Call `CudaDeviceAllocator::EnterStreamCapture` and `CudaDeviceAllocator::ExitStreamCapture` in `CudnnHandle` (`xla/stream_executor/cuda/cuda_dnn.cc`) so that VMM deallocations are deferred until the active cuDNN operation completes.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1003451880

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Cache ContainsSignificantReduce and fast-path non-fusions in FusionInfoCache.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Cache ContainsSignificantReduce and fast-path non-fusions in FusionInfoCache.

In `PriorityFusionQueue::CanFuseWithNativeEmitter`, checking whether a producer or consumer contains a significant reduction (reduction factor >= 16) previously allocated an `HloFusionAdaptor` and traversed all instructions in the fusion on every `(producer, consumer)` pair without caching.

Move this check to `ContainsSignificantReduce` in `gpu_fusible` and cache the result for fusion instructions in `FusionInfoCache` (mirroring `ContainsScan`), guarding against zero-extent reduction output shapes before dividing. Also consolidate `FusionInfoCache` lookups into a shared `GetOrCompute` helper that evaluates non-fusion instructions (`instr.opcode() != HloOpcode::kFusion`) directly without acquiring `mutex_` or populating the cache maps, uses `absl::ReaderMutexLock` for concurrent fusion cache hits, acquires `mutex_` in `Invalidate`, and annotates cache maps with `ABSL_GUARDED_BY(mutex_)`.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 996053044

head_commit.message:
[ROCm] Autotune the MFMA instruction size for Triton GEMMs

Triton picks the largest MFMA that fits the tile, which is not always
the fastest. Let the autotuner also try 16x16 MFMAs so it can pick
whichever is faster.

Tried by default on MI300 only. On MI350, it is limited to exhaustive
search. WMMA targets don't use MFMA.

display_title: PR #51246: [ROCm] Skip the hipGraphGetNodes count in PrepareFinalization on update

head_commit.message:
PR #51246: [ROCm] Skip the hipGraphGetNodes count in PrepareFinalization on update

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51246

## 📝 Summary of Changes

`RocmCommandBuffer::PrepareFinalization()` returns early when the command buffer is being updated, so `Finalize()`
after `Update()` no longer asks HIP for the graph's node count.

## 🎯 Justification

Every time XLA updates a ROCm command buffer, it asks HIP how many nodes the graph has, and it does this right before launching the graph. HIP has no cheap way to answer: it topologically sorts the whole graph just to return the count. The count can't change during an update, so the work is wasted, and it sits on the host's critical path before every updated `hipGraphLaunch`.

Only `Create*` methods add nodes, and they all require `State::kCreate`, so the create-time finalization has already
made the graph non-empty.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

⚡️ Performance Improvement · 🧪 Tests

## 🧪 Unit Tests

`GpuCommandBufferTest.UpdateEmptyCommandBuffer` (`xla/stream_executor/gpu/gpu_command_buffer_test.cc`): an empty
command buffer is finalized, submitted, updated, finalized and submitted again. It covers the ROCm path and is skipped
on CUDA.

name: CI
display_title: Propagate buffer layout constraint across rank-changing bitcast-convert

head_commit.message:
Propagate buffer layout constraint across rank-changing bitcast-convert

When a bitcast-convert instruction adds or removes a trailing dimension and has
rank >= 2, layout assignment read the instruction's existing shape layout
instead of the incoming buffer layout constraint's minor_to_major order.
Instructions lowered from StableHLO do not yet have layouts assigned on their
shapes, so propagating an output constraint crashed on a missing layout check,
and non-default output layout constraints were ignored when an initial layout
was present. Appending a minor dimension during shape inference also asserted in
debug builds that a layout was already present on the shape.

Propagating minor_to_major from the incoming buffer layout constraint without
carrying over element-type-specific layout attributes and allowing optional
layouts when appending a minor dimension fixes compilation of multi-dimensional
cross-width bitcast-convert operations.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1003831271

Also rename a test whose name had double negations.
