name: CI
display_title: Propagate buffer layout constraint across rank-changing bitcast-convert

head_commit.message:
Propagate buffer layout constraint across rank-changing bitcast-convert

When a bitcast-convert instruction adds or removes a trailing dimension and has
rank >= 2, layout assignment read the instruction's existing shape layout
instead of the incoming buffer layout constraint's minor_to_major order.
Instructions lowered from StableHLO do not yet have layouts assigned on their
shapes, so propagating an output constraint crashed on a missing layout check,
and non-default output layout constraints were ignored when an initial layout
was present. Appending a minor dimension during shape inference also asserted in
debug builds that a layout was already present on the shape.

Propagating minor_to_major from the incoming buffer layout constraint without
carrying over element-type-specific layout attributes and allowing optional
layouts when appending a minor dimension fixes compilation of multi-dimensional
cross-width bitcast-convert operations.

name: CI
display_title: [XLA] Speed up HloEvaluator::HandleReduce for integer, tuple, and large-output reductions.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Speed up HloEvaluator::HandleReduce for integer, tuple, and large-output reductions.

Previously, `HloEvaluator::HandleReduce` used a fast path only for single-output floating-point scalar `kAdd` reductions. For integer reductions and variadic tuple reductions, `GenerateReduceOutputElement` ran an embedded `HloEvaluator` on every input element. Each reduction step allocated and destroyed scalar `Literal` objects and called `DecomposeTuple()`. In addition, for every output element, `GenerateReduceOutputElement` and `ShapeUtil::ForEachIndexNoStatus` allocated temporary index `std::vector` objects on the heap. On large reductions across many worker threads, these heap allocations caused high allocator lock contention and 900s test timeouts.

Extend `MatchSimpleBinaryReducer` to match single-output and variadic tuple reductions over simple scalar binary operations (`kAdd`, `kMultiply`, `kMaximum`, `kMinimum`, `kAnd`, `kOr`, `kXor`). Keep chunked `double` accumulation (`GetSumAsDouble`) for floating-point `kAdd` reductions. Evaluate all other matched binary reductions in native types over raw input buffers without heap allocations, and skip creating per-thread `embedded_evaluators`. Precompute linear strides per input argument (`SimpleReducePlan`) to iterate over reduced dimensions without per-output-element heap allocations or multidimensional index conversions. For general reductions that use the embedded evaluator, allocate `arg_values`, `accumulators`, and `embedded_operands` once per output element, and read tuple outputs with `LiteralSlice` instead of `DecomposeTuple()`.

This reduces unsharded `reduce_test_h100` (all 304 tests) runtime from over 2,300s (timeout) to 95.3s:
- `ReduceTestHlo.VariadicLaneAndMajorReductionWithLeadingTrivialDim`: >900s (timeout) to 0.232s
- `ReduceTestHlo.SingleOutputLaneAndMajorReductionWithLeadingTrivialDim`: 120.3s to 0.600s
- `GeneralReduceTest` (150 tests): 1,183.2s to 42.9s

display_title: PR #48089: [XLA:GPU] Fix loop emitter insert point after emitting a loop mid-block

head_commit.message:
PR #48089: [XLA:GPU] Fix loop emitter insert point after emitting a loop mid-block

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/48089

## 📝 Summary of Changes

Fixes #47372.

A sort comparator that computes non-scalar intermediate values crashes GPU
compilation with `llvm_loop.cc:76] Check failed:
!preheader_bb_->hasTerminator()`. The GPU nested computation emitter
(`CodegenNestedComputation`) emits comparators as inline functions with the
builder positioned before a pre-created `ret void`. The first multi-element
op emits its loop through `ForLoop::Emit`'s split path, which moves the
`ret` into the new `loop_exit` block. `LoopEmitter::EmitLoop` (and
`ForLoop::Emit` itself) then reposition the builder at the end of
`loop_exit`, which is after the moved `ret`. The next loop-emitting op sees
an insert point at the end of a terminated block and trips the CHECK.

The fix repositions the builder at the exit block's first insertion point
instead of its end, in both `LoopEmitter::EmitLoop` and `ForLoop::Emit`.
For the common case (the loop was emitted at the end of an unterminated
block, so the exit block is a fresh empty block) this is identical to the
old behavior. For the mid-block split case it puts follow-up code where the
original insertion point was: before whatever the split moved into the exit
block. `ParallelLoopEmitter::EmitLoop` already handles its exit block this
way; the shared llvm_ir helpers never did.

## 🎯 Justification

The module in the issue is valid HLO (plain ops, runs fine on CPU and
interpreter); the GPU backend aborts the whole process while compiling it.
Any custom sort comparator with non-scalar intermediates that survive
simplification hits this, as does any nested call computation emitted
through `CallNestedComputation`. The crash reproduces without any XLA
flags.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

## 🧪 Unit Tests:

`SortTest.MultiElementComparator` in `xla/tests/sort_test.cc`: sorts
`f32[32]` with a comparator that is semantically `p0 < p1` but computed
through `f32[2]` intermediates (iota, two broadcasts, two adds, elementwise
compare, slice, reshape), compared against the interpreter reference with
zero tolerance. Without the fix the GPU test dies on the `llvm_loop.cc:76`
CHECK; with the fix it passes. `sort_test_cpu`, `sort_test_nvgpu_any`, all
`//xla/service/llvm_ir/...` and `//xla/service/cpu/tests/...` targets pass
with the change.

## 🧪 Execution Tests:

The issue's original StableHLO module and a reduced 19-line HLO module both
compile and run on one GPU (RTX 2070, sm_75) with the fix and abort at the
CHECK without it. The fixed binary's outputs match the interpreter
elementwise for order-consistent comparators.
Copybara import of the project:

--
2b030bf33c80fbf195afa04ddbe31f0a17eb24b1 by Stanislav Bardyuk <sbardyuk@google.com>:

[XLA:GPU] Fix loop emitter insert point after emitting a loop mid-block

ForLoop::Emit supports emitting a loop in the middle of a basic block by
splitting it; splitBasicBlock moves the tail of the block, including its
terminator, into the new loop_exit block. But after emitting the loop,
ForLoop::Emit and LoopEmitter::EmitLoop repositioned the builder at the
end of loop_exit, i.e. after the moved terminator. The GPU nested
computation emitter hits exactly this: it emits sort comparators inline
with the builder parked before a pre-created ret. A comparator with two
or more non-scalar intermediate values then crashes on the
llvm_loop.cc:76 CHECK when the second loop is emitted at the end of the
already-terminated loop_exit block.

Reposition the builder at the exit block's first insertion point
instead, which is where the pre-split insertion point's continuation
belongs. For loops emitted at the end of an unterminated block the exit
block is empty and this is identical to the previous behavior.
ParallelLoopEmitter::EmitLoop already handles its exit block this way.

Fixes #47372.

Merging this change closes #48089

head_commit.message:
PR #51324: Bump numpy from 2.4.6 to 2.5.4 Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51324 Bumps [numpy](https://github.com/numpy/numpy) from 2.4.6 to 2.5.4.
Release notes

Sourced from numpy's releases.

v2.5.4 (Oct 10, 2026)

NumPy 2.5.4 Release Notes

Released on 2026-10-10.

NumPy 2.5.4 is a patch release that fixes bugs discovered after the 2.5.3 release. Highlights are:

  • Many typing fixes and improvements,
  • A workaround for the MSVC 19.51 bug, see below.

This release supports Python versions 3.12-3.15.

Improvements

  • numpy.linalg.svd and numpy.linalg.lstsq now raise for inputs containing infinities instead of returning garbage results.

  • Fixed hangs in numpy.linalg.svd and numpy.linalg.lstsq for certain inputs containing infinities for recent versions of some LAPACK implementations.

  • numpy.linalg.cond now handles non-finite inputs more consistently.

(gh-32593)

StringDType hashing with NaN sentinels

StringDType instances with equivalent floating-point NaN sentinels now have equal hashes. Previously, distinct NaN objects could produce equal dtype instances with different hashes, causing dictionary lookups and set deduplication to fail.

(gh-32563)

Changes

MaskedArray resets a fill_value that cannot be represented in a new dtype

A fill_value copied from a source array is now reset to the default fill_value for the new dtype when it cannot be represented in that dtype. Previously the copied value could be stale: ufuncs that change dtype left the result holding a fill_value typed for the old dtype, which raised a TypeError only when something later validated it (such as .view()), and a floating point fill_value that overflows an integer dtype was kept as an out-of-range value together with a RuntimeWarning. Both now fall back to the default, including when a masked array is passed to MaskedArray with a different dtype. A fill_value given explicitly by the user is still validated and raises as before. This can now raise a ComplexWarning if the fill_value is complex and the new dtype is real.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Record symmetric-memory RA2A directly into command buffers.

  - Preload the kernel during Init and not afterwards. Otherwise *dread*locks.
  - Use nice things like command buffer nodes for ra2a instead of tracing.
  - When we use symmetric kernels shift ra2a to DebugOptions::COLLECTIVES_KERNEL so its enabled by default.

v2.5.0

This release moves the action to Scorecard v5.6.0, the first Scorecard release since its hosted services moved to new infrastructure.

  • The action no longer prints the GitHub token variable while validating its options. by @​arpitjain099 in ossf/scorecard-action#1709
  • results_format accepts intoto, which wraps the JSON results in an in-toto attestation statement. by @​puerco in ossf/scorecard-action#1702

Sourced from ossf/scorecard-action's releases.

v2.5.0

What's Changed

This release moves the action to Scorecard v5.6.0, the first Scorecard release since its hosted services moved to new infrastructure.

For changes to checks and results, and what the infrastructure move means for you, see the Scorecard v5.6.0 release notes.

display_title: [Mosaic TPU] Prove divisibility through masks.

head_commit.message:
[Mosaic TPU] Prove divisibility through masks.

Kernels often round sizes and offsets to tiles with a mask, e.g. `(n + 127) & -128`. `isDivisible` could not see through `arith.andi`, so such values needed an explicit `tpu.assume_multiple` before they could slice a tiled dimension.

`isStructurallyDivisible` now proves `x & y` divisible by `2^k` if either operand is, since a mask keeps the low zero bits of both operands. The rule:

* applies only to power-of-two divisors, which covers tile sizes;
* only ever returns `true` or `nullopt`, because `x & y` can be divisible when neither operand is (`5 & 6 == 4`).

So it can prove more values aligned but never rejects anything that verified before.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1003817809

display_title: PR #51324: Bump numpy from 2.4.6 to 2.5.4

head_commit.message:
PR #51324: Bump numpy from 2.4.6 to 2.5.4 Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51324 Bumps [numpy](https://github.com/numpy/numpy) from 2.4.6 to 2.5.4.
Release notes

Sourced from numpy's releases.

v2.5.4 (Oct 10, 2026)

NumPy 2.5.4 Release Notes

Released on 2026-10-10.

NumPy 2.5.4 is a patch release that fixes bugs discovered after the 2.5.3 release. Highlights are:

  • Many typing fixes and improvements,
  • A workaround for the MSVC 19.51 bug, see below.

This release supports Python versions 3.12-3.15.

Improvements

  • numpy.linalg.svd and numpy.linalg.lstsq now raise for inputs containing infinities instead of returning garbage results.

  • Fixed hangs in numpy.linalg.svd and numpy.linalg.lstsq for certain inputs containing infinities for recent versions of some LAPACK implementations.

  • numpy.linalg.cond now handles non-finite inputs more consistently.

(gh-32593)

StringDType hashing with NaN sentinels

StringDType instances with equivalent floating-point NaN sentinels now have equal hashes. Previously, distinct NaN objects could produce equal dtype instances with different hashes, causing dictionary lookups and set deduplication to fail.

(gh-32563)

Changes

MaskedArray resets a fill_value that cannot be represented in a new dtype

A fill_value copied from a source array is now reset to the default fill_value for the new dtype when it cannot be represented in that dtype. Previously the copied value could be stale: ufuncs that change dtype left the result holding a fill_value typed for the old dtype, which raised a TypeError only when something later validated it (such as .view()), and a floating point fill_value that overflows an integer dtype was kept as an out-of-range value together with a RuntimeWarning. Both now fall back to the default, including when a masked array is passed to MaskedArray with a different dtype. A fill_value given explicitly by the user is still validated and raises as before. This can now raise a ComplexWarning if the fill_value is complex and the new dtype is real.

display_title: DEFAULT in `AssignBuffersWithSequentialOrdering` now uses `SPATIAL` instead of BEST_OF_SPATIAL_TEMPORAL, so the heap simulation runs once instead of twice.

head_commit.message:
DEFAULT in `AssignBuffersWithSequentialOrdering` now uses `SPATIAL` instead of BEST_OF_SPATIAL_TEMPORAL, so the heap simulation runs once instead of twice.

BEST_OF_SPATIAL_TEMPORAL can still be requested explicitly.

head_commit.message:
PR #51325: Bump github/codeql-action/upload-sarif from 4.38.1 to 4.38.3 Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51325 Bumps [github/codeql-action/upload-sarif](https://github.com/github/codeql-action) from 4.38.1 to 4.38.3.
Release notes

Sourced from github/codeql-action/upload-sarif's releases.

v4.38.3

  • Upcoming breaking change: CodeQL version 2.21.2 and earlier were discontinued on 24 September 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.17, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. Added a deprecation warning for customers using these versions of CodeQL. #4188
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.2. #4203
  • Fixed a bug where the decision of whether to use a per-language bundle did not account for custom configurations that reference queries outside of compiled CodeQL packs. This issue was caught during internal testing and did not affect any customer repositories. We will resume the roll out of per-language bundles in the coming weeks. #4184

v4.38.2

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.1. #4160
Changelog

Sourced from github/codeql-action/upload-sarif's changelog.

CodeQL Action Changelog

See the releases page for the relevant changes to the CodeQL CLI and language packs.

[UNRELEASED]

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.3. #4256

4.39.0 - 15 Oct 2026

  • Breaking change: Bump the minimum required CodeQL bundle version to 2.20.7. #4205
  • The codeql-action/analyze step now validates that a correct argument for the checkout_path input has been provided. The checkout_path input must be set to the path where the repository that is being analyzed is checked out at on the runner, if that path is something other than the workspace root. If the path does not point to a repository checkout or is different from the path that was used by codeql-action/init, then the CodeQL Action now produces a warning. #4148
  • Resolved an issue with third-party caching implementations that prevented caches from being restored correctly. #4206
  • The codeql-action/start-proxy step that is used in Code Scanning Default Setup now finds CodeQL releases using the same logic as codeql-action/init. This primarily benefits customers who are using GitHub instances other than github.com where the codeql-action/start-proxy step may previously have been unable to locate recent releases and ended up using outdated versions of the private registry authentication proxy as a result. #4198

4.38.3 - 08 Oct 2026

  • Upcoming breaking change: CodeQL version 2.21.2 and earlier were discontinued on 24 September 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.17, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. Added a deprecation warning for customers using these versions of CodeQL. #4188
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.2. #4203
  • Fixed a bug where the decision of whether to use a per-language bundle did not account for custom configurations that reference queries outside of compiled CodeQL packs. This issue was caught during internal testing and did not affect any customer repositories. We will resume the roll out of per-language bundles in the coming weeks. #4184

4.38.2 - 24 Sept 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.1. #4160

4.38.1 - 18 Sept 2026

  • The CodeQL Action now has experimental support for CodeQL releases for which per-language bundles are available. Per-language bundles support analysis for a single language and are therefore smaller than the combined bundles that allow analysis for all supported languages. As a result, per-language bundles take up less space on disk and are faster to download. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in the coming weeks. #4146

4.38.0 - 09 Sept 2026

  • On GitHub-hosted runners, the CodeQL Action now deletes unused CodeQL bundles from the toolcache before downloading a different bundle, which frees up disk space for the analysis. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in September. #4124
  • The CodeQL Action now supports CodeQL releases that are compatible with Linux Arm64 and downloads the native linux-arm64 CodeQL bundle when available. #4072
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.0. #4129

4.37.9 - 26 Aug 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.26.4. #4106

4.37.8 - 21 Aug 2026

No user facing changes.

4.37.7 - 13 Aug 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.26.3. #4085

4.37.6 - 04 Aug 2026

  • Changed the default filepath for the new remote file address format that was introduced in CodeQL Action 4.37.0 / 3.37.0 to .github/codeql-config.yml to align it with the suggested path that is used elsewhere. #4070

head_commit.message:
PR #51324: Bump numpy from 2.4.6 to 2.5.4 Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51324 Bumps [numpy](https://github.com/numpy/numpy) from 2.4.6 to 2.5.4.
Release notes

Sourced from numpy's releases.

v2.5.4 (Oct 10, 2026)

NumPy 2.5.4 Release Notes

Released on 2026-10-10.

NumPy 2.5.4 is a patch release that fixes bugs discovered after the 2.5.3 release. Highlights are:

  • Many typing fixes and improvements,
  • A workaround for the MSVC 19.51 bug, see below.

This release supports Python versions 3.12-3.15.

Improvements

  • numpy.linalg.svd and numpy.linalg.lstsq now raise for inputs containing infinities instead of returning garbage results.

  • Fixed hangs in numpy.linalg.svd and numpy.linalg.lstsq for certain inputs containing infinities for recent versions of some LAPACK implementations.

  • numpy.linalg.cond now handles non-finite inputs more consistently.

(gh-32593)

StringDType hashing with NaN sentinels

StringDType instances with equivalent floating-point NaN sentinels now have equal hashes. Previously, distinct NaN objects could produce equal dtype instances with different hashes, causing dictionary lookups and set deduplication to fail.

(gh-32563)

Changes

MaskedArray resets a fill_value that cannot be represented in a new dtype

A fill_value copied from a source array is now reset to the default fill_value for the new dtype when it cannot be represented in that dtype. Previously the copied value could be stale: ufuncs that change dtype left the result holding a fill_value typed for the old dtype, which raised a TypeError only when something later validated it (such as .view()), and a floating point fill_value that overflows an integer dtype was kept as an out-of-range value together with a RuntimeWarning. Both now fall back to the default, including when a masked array is passed to MaskedArray with a different dtype. A fill_value given explicitly by the user is still validated and raises as before. This can now raise a ComplexWarning if the fill_value is complex and the new dtype is real.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Defer CUDA VMM memory deallocations while a cuDNN handle is active.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Defer CUDA VMM memory deallocations while a cuDNN handle is active.

cuDNN v9 internally captures temporary CUDA graphs during heuristic queries and execution plan creation (e.g. via `cudnn::backend::cudnnBackendGetMetadataFromGraph` inside `cudnnBackendFinalize`), which does not go through `CudaStream::CaptureHandle`.

During parallel autotuning (`ConfigAssigner::GetConfigsForAll`), a worker thread running `GpuProfiler::Profile` can deallocate VMM buffers via `CudaDeviceMemoryAllocation::~CudaDeviceMemoryAllocation` -> `DrainPendingVmmDeallocations` -> `cuCtxSynchronize()` concurrently with the main thread querying cuDNN heuristics in `CudnnSupport::GetConvolveRunners`. Calling `cuCtxSynchronize()` while cuDNN is capturing a CUDA graph on the same CUDA context either fails with `CUDA_ERROR_STREAM_CAPTURE_UNSUPPORTED` / `cudaErrorStreamCaptureInvalidated` or segfaults inside `libcuda.so` (`cuCtxSynchronize`).

Call `CudaDeviceAllocator::EnterStreamCapture` and `CudaDeviceAllocator::ExitStreamCapture` in `CudnnHandle` (`xla/stream_executor/cuda/cuda_dnn.cc`) so that VMM deallocations are deferred until the active cuDNN operation completes.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1003451880

display_title: Deprecate `tsl::strings::LegacyPrecision` in favor of `absl::HighPrecision`.

head_commit.message:
Deprecate `tsl::strings::LegacyPrecision` in favor of `absl::HighPrecision`.

`LegacyPrecision(float)` and `LegacyPrecision(double)` now forward to
`absl::HighPrecision`, and the custom `FpToBuffer` implementation is removed.

This is a value-preserving but not byte-identical change in formatting:
- float: the old implementation used %.6g and fell back to %.9g. absl uses
  the shortest of 6-9 significant digits that round-trips, e.g.
  1.17549435e-38f is now printed as "1.1754944e-38". This matches what the
  header comment already documented (%.6g, %.7g, %.8g, or %.9g).
- double: unchanged (%.15g, falling back to %.17g).
- NaN with the sign bit set is now printed as "nan" instead of "-nan".

All outputs still round-trip to the exact same value.

display_title: PR #51182: [CPU] Coalesce tuple all-reduce buffers for Gloo

head_commit.message:
PR #51182: [CPU] Coalesce tuple all-reduce buffers for Gloo

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51182

# [CPU] Coalesce tuple all-reduce buffers for Gloo

CPU tuple all-reduces currently invoke Gloo once per buffer, paying synchronous ring latency for each parameter even when the compiler combines the operation. This change reduces compatible buffers together.

Fixes #50283.

### Summary of Changes

- Add `Communicator::AllReduceMany` with a default per-buffer implementation and route the CPU all-reduce thunk through it.
- Override the batch operation in Gloo: group buffers deterministically by datatype, pack into aligned temporary storage, perform one reduction per nonempty group, and unpack successful results.
- Preserve the single-buffer direct path and existing behavior for other communicator backends.
- Validate buffer sizes and packed-size overflow, and keep scratch storage alive until the reduction completes.

### Justification

Combined gradient all-reduces with many small buffers pay repeated ring startup latency on CPU hosts. Coalescing buffers reduces collective calls from one per buffer to one per datatype group. Packing adds copies and two temporary buffers for the group being processed.

### Kind of Contribution

CPU tuple all-reduces currently invoke Gloo once per buffer, paying synchronous ring latency for each parameter even when the compiler combines the operation. This change reduces compatible buffers together.

- Validate buffer sizes and packed-size overflow, and keep scratch storage alive until the reduction completes.

head_commit.message:
Follow-up to review comments on cl/1003709391. The indexing cost model's estimates for scan fusions already decrease with the sequential tile size, so the near-tie tie-break towards larger sequential tiles is no longer needed: without it, the tiling search picks the same tiling for 126 of 128 benchmark scan fusions on H100 and B200, and the other two pick a sequential tile of 8192 instead of 16384 at estimates within 0.02%.

Also rename a test whose name had double negations.

Skip a sibling multi-output fusion when one sibling is a column reduction whose grid has fewer blocks than the GPU has cores, and the other sibling is not a reduction.

PR #51300: [Python] Handle 32-bit NumPy shape and stride metadata

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51300

I hit this while building JAX/XLA with Emscripten. `nb_numpy_ndarray` assumes `npy_intp` and `int64_t` have the same width, so its static assertion fails on 32-bit targets.

This converts shape and stride metadata when the widths differ, checking for overflow before passing it to NumPy. The existing 64-bit path stays unchanged.

display_title: Deprecate `tsl::strings::LegacyPrecision` in favor of `absl::HighPrecision`.

head_commit.message:
Deprecate `tsl::strings::LegacyPrecision` in favor of `absl::HighPrecision`.

`LegacyPrecision(float)` and `LegacyPrecision(double)` now forward to
`absl::HighPrecision`, and the custom `FpToBuffer` implementation is removed.

This is a value-preserving but not byte-identical change in formatting:
- float: the old implementation used %.6g and fell back to %.9g. absl uses
  the shortest of 6-9 significant digits that round-trips, e.g.
  1.17549435e-38f is now printed as "1.1754944e-38". This matches what the
  header comment already documented (%.6g, %.7g, %.8g, or %.9g).
- double: unchanged (%.15g, falling back to %.17g).
- NaN with the sign bit set is now printed as "nan" instead of "-nan".

All outputs still round-trip to the exact same value.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1003771966

display_title: PR #51182: [CPU] Coalesce tuple all-reduce buffers for Gloo

head_commit.message:
PR #51182: [CPU] Coalesce tuple all-reduce buffers for Gloo

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51182

# [CPU] Coalesce tuple all-reduce buffers for Gloo

CPU tuple all-reduces currently invoke Gloo once per buffer, paying synchronous ring latency for each parameter even when the compiler combines the operation. This change reduces compatible buffers together.

Fixes #50283.

### Summary of Changes

- Add `Communicator::AllReduceMany` with a default per-buffer implementation and route the CPU all-reduce thunk through it.
- Override the batch operation in Gloo: group buffers deterministically by datatype, pack into aligned temporary storage, perform one reduction per nonempty group, and unpack successful results.
- Preserve the single-buffer direct path and existing behavior for other communicator backends.
- Validate buffer sizes and packed-size overflow, and keep scratch storage alive until the reduction completes.

### Justification

Combined gradient all-reduces with many small buffers pay repeated ring startup latency on CPU hosts. Coalescing buffers reduces collective calls from one per buffer to one per datatype group. Packing adds copies and two temporary buffers for the group being processed.

### Kind of Contribution

Bug Fix, Performance Improvement, Tests.

### Benchmark

End-to-end JAX timings and the public-HLO benchmark requested by this template have not been measured. No measured speedup is claimed. A regression test verifies the reduction in underlying collective calls.

### Unit Tests

Added tests for datatype grouping and collective-call counts, the default fallback, empty and single-buffer inputs, error propagation, oversized counts, and avoiding unpacking after a failed reduction.

### Execution Tests

Added a two-rank Gloo test covering mixed float/integer buffers, SUM/PRODUCT/MIN/MAX reductions, and separate versus in-place outputs.

Validation on Ubuntu/WSL with Clang 18 and Bazel 8.7.0 (`--config=clang_local -c fastbuild`):

- `//xla/backends/cpu/collectives:gloo_collectives_test`: all 186 tests passed, including the four new regression tests.
- `//xla/backends/cpu/runtime:all_reduce_thunk`: built successfully.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

PR #50857: [XLA:GPU] Skip sibling fusion into small column reductions

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50857

📝 Summary of Changes

Skip a sibling multi-output fusion when one sibling is a column reduction whose grid has fewer blocks than the GPU has cores, and the other sibling is not a reduction.

🎯 Justification

Merging would run the non-reduction sibling on the reduction's small grid, which is slower than keeping them as two separate fusions.

🚀 Kind of Contribution:⚡️ Performance Improvement,

📊 Benchmark

detr -3%, and lit/lip/siglip/gemma3_4b ~-1% on MI300 and MI350

head_commit.message:
Allow `PriorityFusion` to fuse producers into Triton scan fusions whose scans have a scan dimension of at most 128 (`kMaxRowLocalScanDimSize`). The row then fits into a single tile, so row-wise producers such as a softmax can be fused. For example, the softmax of a top-p sampling mask (softmax, cumsum, compare and select) can then be fused into the scan.

`FusionBlockLevelRewriter` re-tiles fusions whose sequential tile sizes no longer match their tiling space, e.g. after `HloCSE` merged reduces that producer fusion had duplicated.

With default flags, this change has no effect.

[XLA:GPU] Remove persistent symmetric memory copy skipping in GPU collective buffer analysis.

Skipping defensive copies for module-boundary buffers in collective memory space (`kCollectiveMemorySpaceColor`) under `--xla_gpu_enable_persistent_symmetric_memory` is unsafe because caller-provided input buffers and returned output buffers are allocated by the host/PJRT allocator in default device memory rather than symmetric collective memory.

name: CI
display_title: Preserve `stack_frame_index` when embedding computations in `XlaBuilder`.

head_commit.message:
Preserve `stack_frame_index` when embedding computations in `XlaBuilder`.

`XlaBuilder::AddSubComputation` copied the embedded computation's
`HloComputationProto`s but dropped its `stack_frame_index`, leaving the
instructions' `stack_frame_id`s dangling. `HloModule::CanonicalizeStackFrameIds`
then reset them to 0, so source locations were lost for any computation built
via `ConvertMlirHloToHlo` and then embedded through `xla::Call`.

`XlaBuilder` now keeps a `StackFrames` table for imported computations:

-   `AddSubComputation` re-interns each imported frame (and its parent chain)
    into it, so identical frames are stored once, and rewrites the imported
    instructions' ids accordingly.
-   `BuildSubComputation` re-interns a child builder's table into its parent, only for entries that were imported with a stack frame index.
-   `Build()` / `BuildConstantSubGraph()` emit it as the module's
    `stack_frame_index`.
-   Ids set directly via `SetOpMetadata` (i.e. on the builder's own
    instructions, or on imported computations that carry no table) refer to a
    caller-owned table and are left untouched.

display_title: PR #50907: [XLA:GPU] Fix PGLE handling of fusions and async compute.

head_commit.message:
PR #50907: [XLA:GPU] Fix PGLE handling of fusions and async compute.

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50907

📝 Summary of Changes

Estimate PGLE costs of fusions from their wrapped instructions if there is no entry for the fusion itself.

🎯 Justification

For example, this fixes latency lookup of dynamic slice fusions, whose runtime is attributed to the wrapped instructions in profile data.

This showed up in DSv3 training with TransformerEngine custom calls, where fused backward attention kernels received fallback costs rather than PGLE measurements.

Also fix an analogous issue with async computations, as emitted by compute_on APIs.

Using the measured costs allows for better scheduling decisions.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix, ⚡️ Performance Improvement

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)

DSv3 training on GB300 showed an O(5%) improvement in step time due to better scheduling flowing from this change.

This fires on the `hlo_llama3_8b_bf16_activation_offloading_1x8.hlo` benchmark HLO, giving 0.4% speedup on an 8xH100 node.

🧪 Unit Tests:

Unit test added.

🧪 Execution Tests:

n/a
Copybara import of the project:

92a460687e87e4f6e9e689f793fb90230238207f by Olli Lupton <olupton@nvidia.com>:

[XLA:GPU] Fix PGLE handling of async compute.

There are two variants on the same theme of PGLE failing to find
measured costs for an instruction because the device-side work measured
in the profile is attributed to wrapped instructions rather than the
top-level ones:
- fusions: use the sum of measured costs for the instructions it
  contains, for example fixing the case of dynamic slice fusions where
  the wrapped custom call (for example) is what appears in the profile
- async compute: previously these were not considered as the relevant
  code path only considered collectives. This fixes, for example,
  work on parallel streams coming from use of JAX's compute_on API.

Merging this change closes #50907

Deprecate `tsl::strings::LegacyPrecision` in favor of `absl::HighPrecision`.

`LegacyPrecision(float)` and `LegacyPrecision(double)` now forward to
`absl::HighPrecision`, and the custom `FpToBuffer` implementation is removed.

This is a value-preserving but not byte-identical change in formatting:
- float: the old implementation used %.6g and fell back to %.9g. absl uses
  the shortest of 6-9 significant digits that round-trips, e.g.
  1.17549435e-38f is now printed as "1.1754944e-38". This matches what the
  header comment already documented (%.6g, %.7g, %.8g, or %.9g).
- double: unchanged (%.15g, falling back to %.17g).
- NaN with the sign bit set is now printed as "nan" instead of "-nan".

display_title: [XLA] Treat block-scale dequantized weights as parameter-like in dot swapping

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Treat block-scale dequantized weights as parameter-like in dot swapping

- `AlgebraicSimplifierVisitor::MoveDotParamToRhs` swaps `dot(activations,
  weights)` when `enable_move_dot_param_to_rhs` is enabled and only the LHS
  looks parameter-like, which breaks RHS-only convolution input fusion when the
  weight goes through a block-scaled dequantization graph (`reshape ->
  multiply(broadcast(scale)) -> reshape -> convert`).
- Extend `IsParameterLike` to look through elementwise ops where all but one
  operand is a broadcast (through bitcast/reshape/convert) of a parameter-like
  subtree (bounded to depth 4).
- Add unit test `DontSwapDotOperandsWithDequantizedWeight`.

name: CI
display_title: Speed up Clang-Tidy, DWYU, and query CI workflows

head_commit.message:
Speed up Clang-Tidy, DWYU, and query CI workflows

The Clang-Tidy, DWYU, and Bazel query/lint workflows in GitHub Actions currently repeat full-repository analysis or do unnecessary work on every pull request:

1. In `clang_tidy.yml` and `run_clang_tidy.sh`, the workflow invokes `./configure.py` (which is meant for local developer setups rather than CI) and writes `build:cuda` and `test --test_env` flags into `xla_configure.bazelrc` that cause `bazel build` to discard the `bazel cquery` analysis cache. In addition, `xla_test` expands into up to 10 backend `cc_test` variants that compile the same sources, non-test `ClangTidy` actions sent to RBE spend ~60s per action uploading `@llvm20_linux_x86_64//:all` and run slower on 1-vCPU RBE workers than on the 16-vCPU runner VM, and `bazel run //build_tools/ci:clang_tidy_diff` triggers a third Bazel invocation even when `--fix` is not set.
2. In `dwyu.yml`, the workflow fetches all branches (`fetch-depth: 0`) and runs `bazelisk build --nobuild //xla/...` across all XLA packages before running `check_dwyu.py` to see whether any C++ targets were modified.
3. In `bazel_dependency_violations.yml`, `bazel_query.yml`, and `bazel_tags.yml`, each job runs `bazel build --nobuild //xla/...` before running `bazel cquery` or `bazel query //xla/...`, which analyzes the entire repository a second time (or runs full configured-target analysis when `bazel query` only needs package loading).

Therefore this change:

1. Replaces `./configure.py` in `clang_tidy.yml` with the fixed `--config rbe_linux_cpu --config cuda_nvcc --config nonccl` configs (passed via a new `--config` flag on `run_clang_tidy.sh` to both `bazel cquery` and `bazel build`), deduplicates `xla_test` backend variants in `run_clang_tidy.sh`, sets `--strategy=ClangTidy=local` so `ClangTidy` aspect actions run directly on the 16-vCPU runner VM while keeping prerequisite build actions on RBE cache, and runs `clang_tidy_diff.py` directly with `python3` when `--fix` is not enabled.
2. Checks out with `fetch-depth: 100` in `dwyu.yml`, runs `check_dwyu.py` before installing `bant` (with SHA-256 verification) or `bazelisk` so PRs without modified C++ targets exit immediately, and scopes `bazelisk build --nobuild` to the packages of the modified targets rather than `//xla/...`.
3. Removes the redundant `bazel build --nobuild //xla/...` step from `bazel_dependency_violations.yml`, `bazel_query.yml`, and `bazel_tags.yml` (downloader retries are already handled by `--experimental_repository_downloader_retries=5`), and skips the `bazel cquery` step in `bazel_dependency_violations.yml` on PRs that do not touch `BUILD`, `.bzl`, `WORKSPACE`, `MODULE.bazel`, or `.bazelrc` files.

Measured wall-clock job durations on PR #51376 (no C++ changes) and PR #51377 (modifying the same two C++ files as PR #50787: `xla/backends/gpu/autotuner/triton/dot_search_space.cc` and `xla/backends/gpu/codegen/triton/tests/scaled_dot_device_test.cc`) compared to PR #50787 and PR #51241:

- `Clang Tidy`:
  - 2-file C++ change (PR #51377 vs. PR #50787): **8m04s** (down from **15m32s**, **48% faster**). `bazel build` reuses the `cquery` analysis cache (analyzing in 0.8s-4.6s instead of 87s), deduplicates `scaled_dot_device_test` variants from 3 targets to 1, runs `ClangTidy` locally without the ~60s RBE upload stall, and runs `clang_tidy_diff.py` in 0.08s without a third Bazel invocation.
  - No C++ changes (PR #51376): **24s**.
- `DWYU (Depend on What You Use)`:
  - 2-file C++ change (PR #51377 vs. PR #50787): **1m53s** (down from **5m33s**, **66% faster**), analyzing 696 targets across the 2 modified packages in 96s instead of 15,729 targets across `//xla/...` in 202s.
  - No C++ changes (PR #51376 vs. PR #51241): **14s** (down from **5m18s**, **96% faster**).
- `Bazel Dependency Violations` (3 matrix jobs):
  - When build or `.bazelrc` files change (PR #51376 and PR #51377 vs. PR #50787): **3m19s-4m27s** (down from **6m28s-6m32s**, **32-49% faster**).
  - When no `BUILD`, `.bzl`, `WORKSPACE`, `MODULE.bazel`, or `.bazelrc` files change: skips `bazel cquery` in **~15s**.
- `Bazel Tags`: **1m04s-1m43s** (down from **3m18s** on PR #50787, **48-68% faster**).
- `Bazel Query`: **2m47s-3m12s** (down from **3m40s** on PR #50787, **13-24% faster**).

name: CI
display_title: Avoid redundant analysis and RBE downloads in CI

head_commit.message:
Avoid redundant analysis and RBE downloads in CI

In `build_tools/ci/build.py` we used to run a separate `bazel build --nobuild` step before the actual `bazel build` or `bazel test` invocation to retry repository fetches. This added a second target-analysis pass (~5-30s on most builds, and ~2.5 min on `Hermetic ROCm` where `+rocm_configure_ext` re-evaluated the main repo mapping) plus BES upload overhead.

Instead let's configure `--experimental_repository_downloader_retries=5` in `tensorflow.bazelrc` so Bazel retries transient download errors in-process without a second invocation, and remove `bazel build --nobuild` from `build_tools/ci/build.py`.

Also:

1. Switch `common:rbe_base` in `tensorflow.bazelrc` (and the Linux JAX RBE builds in `build_tools/ci/build.py`) to `--remote_download_minimal` and `--nobuild_runfile_links` so CI shards still compile and link all non-test binaries on RBE without downloading them or materializing runfiles symlink trees when they are not executed locally.
2. Keep `--remote_download_toplevel` and `--build_runfile_links` enabled for the benchmark presubmit builds (which execute the built binaries from `bazel-bin`) and `--remote_download_toplevel` for `clang-tidy-common` (which reads the generated `.clang-tidy.yaml` files from disk).

Comparing full builds with a warm RBE cache (https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50787 vs. https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51241), this reduces `Run build.py` times across RBE jobs:

- `XLA Linux x86 GPU Hermetic ROCm` (always full build): 11m 49s -> 6m 08s (-2m 38s from removing `--nobuild`, -2m 59s in execution/download phase)
- `XLA Linux X86 GPU ONEAPI` (always full build): 4m 36s -> 3m 49s (-43s in execution/download phase)
- `JAX Linux x86 GPU T4` (always full build): 2m 27s -> 2m 09s (-16s in execution/download phase)
- `XLA Linux x86 CPU WORKSPACE` (full build, warm RBE cache): 7m 54s -> 2m 22s (execution/download phase drops from 6m 27s to 59s; 3,811 fewer `.runfiles` actions)
- `XLA Linux x86 GPU T4` (full build, warm RBE cache): 7m 53s -> 3m 41s (execution/download phase drops from 5m 35s to 1m 08s; 3,029 fewer `.runfiles` actions)

[XLA] Treat block-scale dequantized weights as parameter-like in dot swapping

  fusion when the weight goes through a block-scaled dequantization graph

  operand is a broadcast (through bitcast/reshape/convert) of a parameter-like
  subtree (bounded to depth 4).

name: CI
display_title: Preserve `stack_frame_index` when embedding computations in `XlaBuilder`.

head_commit.message:
Preserve `stack_frame_index` when embedding computations in `XlaBuilder`.

`XlaBuilder::AddSubComputation` copied the embedded computation's
`HloComputationProto`s but dropped its `stack_frame_index`, leaving the
instructions' `stack_frame_id`s dangling. `HloModule::CanonicalizeStackFrameIds`
then reset them to 0, so source locations were lost for any computation built
via `ConvertMlirHloToHlo` and then embedded through `xla::Call`.

`XlaBuilder` now keeps a `StackFrames` table for imported computations:

-   `AddSubComputation` re-interns each imported frame (and its parent chain)
    into it, so identical frames are stored once, and rewrites the imported
    instructions' ids accordingly.
-   `BuildSubComputation` re-interns a child builder's table into its parent, only for entries that were imported with a stack frame index.
-   `Build()` / `BuildConstantSubGraph()` emit it as the module's
    `stack_frame_index`.
-   Ids set directly via `SetOpMetadata` (i.e. on the builder's own
    instructions, or on imported computations that carry no table) refer to a
    caller-owned table and are left untouched.

display_title: Allow in place buffer sharing through kCopyDone in HeapSimulator

head_commit.message:
Allow in place buffer sharing through kCopyDone in HeapSimulator

In HloDataflowAnalysis, kCopyDone forwards the HloValue defined at kCopyStart
index {0}. When DecreasingSizeRunsHeap checks whether an instruction can share
its operand buffer in place, it tests whether the instruction is a direct user
of the HloValue's defining instruction. Because a consumer of kCopyDone has
kCopyDone as its operand rather than kCopyStart, in place buffer sharing never
fired across asynchronous copies and forced two disjoint buffers to remain
simultaneously live.

Recognize operands that are a kCopyDone of the defining kCopyStart{0} value and
pass the kCopyDone instruction to CanShareOperandBufferWithUser so elementwise
and fusion consumers can reuse the destination buffer of an asynchronous copy in
place.

Tests:
- //third_party/tensorflow/compiler/xla/service/heap_simulator:heap_simulator_test
PiperOrigin-RevId: 1004542530

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Strength-reduce one-hot dots into gather and select.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Strength-reduce one-hot dots into gather and select.

Multiplying a one-hot matrix by a weight table `W` is just a row lookup.
Rewrite it as a gather + select. For now its turned off by default. The numbers in the CL are taken with the child CL which turns it on by default. This is just to keep rollback churn low. I want to have it unconditionally later.

Also:
- If the weight is a `reshape(broadcast(param))` on non-contracting
  dimensions (e.g. broadcasting `param[256, 16, 512]` to `[256, 65536]`),
  gather first and apply the `broadcast` + `reshape` afterward so we don't
  gather 8x the data.
- Skip F32 dots with default (TF32) precision so TF32 GEMM numerics do not
  change.

display_title: Add the debug option `xla_gpu_experimental_enable_triton_scan` (default off). When it is set, `GpuCompiler` runs `ScanRewriterTriton` before `AssociativeScanRewriter`, so eligible associative `kScan` instructions become Triton scan fusions instead of reduce-window trees.

head_commit.message:
Add the debug option `xla_gpu_experimental_enable_triton_scan` (default off). When it is set, `GpuCompiler` runs `ScanRewriterTriton` before `AssociativeScanRewriter`, so eligible associative `kScan` instructions become Triton scan fusions instead of reduce-window trees.

The rewriter only sets the fusion kind to `__triton`; the tiling is chosen later by `PriorityFusion`, `FusionBlockLevelRewriter` or the autotuner.

Eligible scans have rank 1 or 2 with the scan dimension last, and the rewriter does nothing on GPUs that Triton does not support. A tiled scan computes one row per block, so scans with a dimension of at least 32768 also need at least 64 rows (`kMinParallelElements`); otherwise the hierarchical scan of `AssociativeScanRewriter` is faster (crossover at 64 rows on H100 and 32 on B200). Shorter scans are faster with Triton at any batch size.

For a cumsum with an elementwise epilogue on f32[B, N], with B from 1 to 256 and N from 1024 to 262144, enabling the flag is never slower on H100 and B200. It is 1.05–2.9x (H100) and 1.06–2.8x (B200) faster for N < 32768, and up to 1.9x (H100) and 2.3x (B200) faster for N ≥ 32768 and B ≥ 64.

A top-p sampling mask (softmax, cumsum, compare and select) on f32[B, K] with B from 1 to 256 and K in {64, 128} compiles to a single Triton kernel: 1.3–1.5 µs instead of 3.3–4.5 µs on H100, and 2.5–3.1 µs instead of 5.9–8.4 µs on B200.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 982293610

display_title: Fix base dilation overlap in SpaceToBatchConverter

head_commit.message:
Fix base dilation overlap in SpaceToBatchConverter

When inherent_low_padding equals base_dilation_factor, SpaceToBatchConverter prepends one undilated element to each split and sets low_padding_for_conv to 0.

For each split of S undilated elements to produce S * base_dilation_factor outputs, the high-side overlap must be kernel_spatial_dim_size + base_dilation_factor - 2 rather than kernel_spatial_dim_size (which only matched for base_dilation_factor == 2). Therefore this change updates last_overlap in GetConvolutionDetails accordingly.

Fixes https://github.com/openxla/xla/issues/51365

head_commit.message:
PR #51324: Bump numpy from 2.4.6 to 2.5.4 Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51324 Bumps [numpy](https://github.com/numpy/numpy) from 2.4.6 to 2.5.4.
Release notes

Sourced from numpy's releases.

v2.5.4 (Oct 10, 2026)

NumPy 2.5.4 Release Notes

Released on 2026-10-10.

NumPy 2.5.4 is a patch release that fixes bugs discovered after the 2.5.3 release. Highlights are:

  • Many typing fixes and improvements,
  • A workaround for the MSVC 19.51 bug, see below.

This release supports Python versions 3.12-3.15.

Improvements

  • numpy.linalg.svd and numpy.linalg.lstsq now raise for inputs containing infinities instead of returning garbage results.

  • Fixed hangs in numpy.linalg.svd and numpy.linalg.lstsq for certain inputs containing infinities for recent versions of some LAPACK implementations.

  • numpy.linalg.cond now handles non-finite inputs more consistently.

(gh-32593)

StringDType hashing with NaN sentinels

StringDType instances with equivalent floating-point NaN sentinels now have equal hashes. Previously, distinct NaN objects could produce equal dtype instances with different hashes, causing dictionary lookups and set deduplication to fail.

(gh-32563)

Changes

MaskedArray resets a fill_value that cannot be represented in a new dtype

A fill_value copied from a source array is now reset to the default fill_value for the new dtype when it cannot be represented in that dtype. Previously the copied value could be stale: ufuncs that change dtype left the result holding a fill_value typed for the old dtype, which raised a TypeError only when something later validated it (such as .view()), and a floating point fill_value that overflows an integer dtype was kept as an out-of-range value together with a RuntimeWarning. Both now fall back to the default, including when a masked array is passed to MaskedArray with a different dtype. A fill_value given explicitly by the user is still validated and raises as before. This can now raise a ComplexWarning if the fill_value is complex and the new dtype is real.

... (truncated)

name: CI
display_title: Avoid redundant analysis and RBE downloads in CI

head_commit.message:
Avoid redundant analysis and RBE downloads in CI

In `build_tools/ci/build.py` we used to run a separate `bazel build --nobuild` step before the actual `bazel build` or `bazel test` invocation to retry repository fetches. This added a second target-analysis pass (~5-30s on most builds, and ~2.5 min on `Hermetic ROCm` where `+rocm_configure_ext` re-evaluated the main repo mapping) plus BES upload overhead.

Instead let's configure `--experimental_repository_downloader_retries=5` in `tensorflow.bazelrc` so Bazel retries transient download errors in-process without a second invocation, and remove `bazel build --nobuild` from `build_tools/ci/build.py`.

Also:

1. Switch `common:rbe_base` in `tensorflow.bazelrc` (and the Linux JAX RBE builds in `build_tools/ci/build.py`) to `--remote_download_minimal` and `--nobuild_runfile_links` so CI shards still compile and link all non-test binaries on RBE without downloading them or materializing runfiles symlink trees when they are not executed locally.
2. Keep `--remote_download_toplevel` and `--build_runfile_links` enabled for the benchmark presubmit builds (which execute the built binaries from `bazel-bin`) and `--remote_download_toplevel` for `clang-tidy-common` (which reads the generated `.clang-tidy.yaml` files from disk).

Comparing full builds with a warm RBE cache (https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50787 vs. https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51241), this reduces `Run build.py` times across RBE jobs:

- `XLA Linux x86 GPU Hermetic ROCm` (always full build): 11m 49s -> 6m 08s (-2m 38s from removing `--nobuild`, -2m 59s in execution/download phase)
- `XLA Linux X86 GPU ONEAPI` (always full build): 4m 36s -> 3m 49s (-43s in execution/download phase)
- `JAX Linux x86 GPU T4` (always full build): 2m 27s -> 2m 09s (-16s in execution/download phase)
- `XLA Linux x86 CPU WORKSPACE` (full build, warm RBE cache): 7m 54s -> 2m 22s (execution/download phase drops from 6m 27s to 59s; 3,811 fewer `.runfiles` actions)

PR #49450: [ROCm] Autotune the MFMA instruction size for Triton GEMMs

📝 Summary of Changes
Add `mfma_size` to the Triton GEMM config and autotune it on MFMA targets. MI300 default configs get `mfma_size: 16` variants. MI350 tries them only in exhaustive search.

🎯 Justification
The auto MFMA choice is often not the fastest on MI300.

🚀 Kind of Contribution:⚡️ Performance Improvement,

[ROCm] Autotune the MFMA instruction size for Triton GEMMs

Triton picks the largest MFMA that fits the tile, which is not always
the fastest. Let the autotuner also try 16x16 MFMAs so it can pick
whichever is faster.

Tried by default on MI300 only. On MI350, it is limited to exhaustive

display_title: PR #50583: [ROCm] [CUDA] Serve pinned_host buffers from host memory with the VMM allocator PR 3/3

head_commit.message:
PR #50583: [ROCm] [CUDA] Serve pinned_host buffers from host memory with the VMM allocator PR 3/3

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50583

Note on these PR chains:  diff here shows +877 lines because it has other two commits combined here , once those two PRs go in actual diff here is only +284. also all three PRs touch shared XLA GPU code.

## 📝 Summary of Changes

With the VMM allocator (`GpuAllocatorConfig::Kind::kVmm`), `pinned_host` buffers now come from pinned host memory instead of device memory, on CUDA and ROCm.

- The PJRT GPU client passes the VMM allocator the same per-device pinned host allocators the BFC path uses. It creates the allocator through the generic `DeviceAddressVmmAllocator::Create()`, so there are no CUDA/ROCm `#if` branches.
- Without a host allocator, `MemorySpace::kHost` requests now fail with `FailedPrecondition` instead of silently getting device memory.

Part 3 of 3; needs both:
1. https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50581: VA remapping skips host memory space allocations
2. https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50582: the VMM allocator serves `MemorySpace::kHost` from a host allocator
3. This PR. **Until PR 1 and PR 2 land, this branch also has their commits; only the last commit is new.**

## 🎯 Justification

For `kVmm`, nothing served the host memory space, so `pinned_host` buffers got device memory with no CPU mapping and any CPU access segfaulted. Orbax checkpointing does exactly that, so every JAX job with `XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_ALLOCATOR=vmm` crashed at its first checkpoint save, on CUDA and ROCm. Command buffer update modes other than `ALWAYS_UPDATE` force the VMM allocator, so they crashed too.

VMM clients now behave like BFC clients for `pinned_host`: the same host memory limit (`XLA_PJRT_GPU_HOST_MEMORY_LIMIT_GB`) and preallocation setting apply, and host offloading actually moves data to host memory.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix, 🧪 Tests

## 🧪 Unit Tests

- `se_gpu_pjrt_client_test`: with VMM, a `pinned_host` buffer created from host data and a `pinned_host` program output are readable on the CPU.
- `se_gpu_pjrt_client_multi_gpu_test`: `pinned_host` buffers on two devices are readable on the CPU.
- `device_address_vmm_allocator_test`: `kHost` without a host allocator fails.

[XLA:GPU] Strength-reduce one-hot dots into gather and select.

Multiplying a one-hot matrix by a weight table `W` is just a row lookup.
Rewrite it as a gather + select.

Also:
- If the weight is a `reshape(broadcast(param))` on non-contracting
  dimensions (e.g. broadcasting `param[256, 16, 512]` to `[256, 65536]`),
  gather first and apply the `broadcast` + `reshape` afterward so we don't
  gather 8x the data.
- Skip F32 dots with default (TF32) precision so TF32 GEMM numerics do not
  change.

head_commit.message:
PR #51324: Bump numpy from 2.4.6 to 2.5.4 Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51324 Bumps [numpy](https://github.com/numpy/numpy) from 2.4.6 to 2.5.4.
Release notes

Sourced from numpy's releases.

v2.5.4 (Oct 10, 2026)

NumPy 2.5.4 Release Notes

Released on 2026-10-10.

NumPy 2.5.4 is a patch release that fixes bugs discovered after the 2.5.3 release. Highlights are:

  • Many typing fixes and improvements,
  • A workaround for the MSVC 19.51 bug, see below.

This release supports Python versions 3.12-3.15.

Improvements

  • numpy.linalg.svd and numpy.linalg.lstsq now raise for inputs containing infinities instead of returning garbage results.

  • Fixed hangs in numpy.linalg.svd and numpy.linalg.lstsq for certain inputs containing infinities for recent versions of some LAPACK implementations.

  • numpy.linalg.cond now handles non-finite inputs more consistently.

(gh-32593)

StringDType hashing with NaN sentinels

StringDType instances with equivalent floating-point NaN sentinels now have equal hashes. Previously, distinct NaN objects could produce equal dtype instances with different hashes, causing dictionary lookups and set deduplication to fail.

(gh-32563)

Changes

MaskedArray resets a fill_value that cannot be represented in a new dtype

A fill_value copied from a source array is now reset to the default fill_value for the new dtype when it cannot be represented in that dtype. Previously the copied value could be stale: ufuncs that change dtype left the result holding a fill_value typed for the old dtype, which raised a TypeError only when something later validated it (such as .view()), and a floating point fill_value that overflows an integer dtype was kept as an out-of-range value together with a RuntimeWarning. Both now fall back to the default, including when a masked array is passed to MaskedArray with a different dtype. A fill_value given explicitly by the user is still validated and raises as before. This can now raise a ComplexWarning if the fill_value is complex and the new dtype is real.

display_title: Add the debug option `xla_gpu_experimental_enable_triton_scan` (default off). When it is set, `GpuCompiler` runs `ScanRewriterTriton` before `AssociativeScanRewriter`, so eligible associative `kScan` instructions become Triton scan fusions instead of reduce-window trees.

head_commit.message:
Add the debug option `xla_gpu_experimental_enable_triton_scan` (default off). When it is set, `GpuCompiler` runs `ScanRewriterTriton` before `AssociativeScanRewriter`, so eligible associative `kScan` instructions become Triton scan fusions instead of reduce-window trees.

The rewriter only sets the fusion kind to `__triton`; the tiling is chosen later by `PriorityFusion`, `FusionBlockLevelRewriter` or the autotuner.

Eligible scans have rank 1 or 2 with the scan dimension last, and the rewriter does nothing on GPUs that Triton does not support. A tiled scan computes one row per block, so scans with a dimension of at least 32768 also need at least 64 rows (`kMinParallelElements`); otherwise the hierarchical scan of `AssociativeScanRewriter` is faster (crossover at 64 rows on H100 and 32 on B200). Shorter scans are faster with Triton at any batch size.

For a cumsum with an elementwise epilogue on f32[B, N], with B from 1 to 256 and N from 1024 to 262144, enabling the flag is never slower on H100 and B200. It is 1.05–2.9x (H100) and 1.06–2.8x (B200) faster for N < 32768, and up to 1.9x (H100) and 2.3x (B200) faster for N ≥ 32768 and B ≥ 64.

A top-p sampling mask (softmax, cumsum, compare and select) on f32[B, K] with B from 1 to 256 and K in {64, 128} compiles to a single Triton kernel: 1.3–1.5 µs instead of 3.3–4.5 µs on H100, and 2.5–3.1 µs instead of 5.9–8.4 µs on B200.

display_title: Fix base dilation overlap in SpaceToBatchConverter

head_commit.message:
Fix base dilation overlap in SpaceToBatchConverter

When inherent_low_padding equals base_dilation_factor, SpaceToBatchConverter prepends one undilated element to each split and sets low_padding_for_conv to 0.

For each split of S undilated elements to produce S * base_dilation_factor outputs, the high-side overlap must be kernel_spatial_dim_size + base_dilation_factor - 2 rather than kernel_spatial_dim_size (which only matched for base_dilation_factor == 2). Therefore this change updates last_overlap in GetConvolutionDetails accordingly.

Fixes https://github.com/openxla/xla/issues/51365

name: CI
display_title: Speed up Clang-Tidy, DWYU, and query CI workflows

head_commit.message:
Speed up Clang-Tidy, DWYU, and query CI workflows

The Clang-Tidy, DWYU, and Bazel query/lint workflows in GitHub Actions currently repeat full-repository analysis or do unnecessary work on every pull request:

1. In `clang_tidy.yml` and `run_clang_tidy.sh`, the workflow invokes `./configure.py` (which is meant for local developer setups rather than CI) and writes `build:cuda` and `test --test_env` flags into `xla_configure.bazelrc` that cause `bazel build` to discard the `bazel cquery` analysis cache. In addition, `xla_test` expands into up to 10 backend `cc_test` variants that compile the same sources, non-test `ClangTidy` actions sent to RBE spend ~60s per action uploading `@llvm20_linux_x86_64//:all` and run slower on 1-vCPU RBE workers than on the 16-vCPU runner VM, and `bazel run //build_tools/ci:clang_tidy_diff` triggers a third Bazel invocation even when `--fix` is not set.
2. In `dwyu.yml`, the workflow fetches all branches (`fetch-depth: 0`) and runs `bazelisk build --nobuild //xla/...` across all XLA packages before running `check_dwyu.py` to see whether any C++ targets were modified.
3. In `bazel_dependency_violations.yml`, `bazel_query.yml`, and `bazel_tags.yml`, each job runs `bazel build --nobuild //xla/...` before running `bazel cquery` or `bazel query //xla/...`, which analyzes the entire repository a second time (or runs full configured-target analysis when `bazel query` only needs package loading).

Therefore this change:

1. Replaces `./configure.py` in `clang_tidy.yml` with the fixed `--config rbe_linux_cpu --config cuda_nvcc --config nonccl` configs (passed via a new `--config` flag on `run_clang_tidy.sh` to both `bazel cquery` and `bazel build`), deduplicates `xla_test` backend variants in `run_clang_tidy.sh`, sets `--strategy=ClangTidy=local` so `ClangTidy` aspect actions run directly on the 16-vCPU runner VM while keeping prerequisite build actions on RBE cache, and runs `clang_tidy_diff.py` directly with `python3` when `--fix` is not enabled.
2. Checks out with `fetch-depth: 100` in `dwyu.yml`, runs `check_dwyu.py` before installing `bant` (with SHA-256 verification) or `bazelisk` so PRs without modified C++ targets exit immediately, and scopes `bazelisk build --nobuild` to the packages of the modified targets rather than `//xla/...`.
3. Removes the redundant `bazel build --nobuild //xla/...` step from `bazel_dependency_violations.yml`, `bazel_query.yml`, and `bazel_tags.yml` (downloader retries are already handled by `--experimental_repository_downloader_retries=5`), and skips the `bazel cquery` step in `bazel_dependency_violations.yml` on PRs that do not touch `BUILD`, `.bzl`, `WORKSPACE`, `MODULE.bazel`, or `.bazelrc` files.

Measured wall-clock job durations on PR #51376 (no C++ changes) and PR #51377 (modifying the same two C++ files as PR #50787: `xla/backends/gpu/autotuner/triton/dot_search_space.cc` and `xla/backends/gpu/codegen/triton/tests/scaled_dot_device_test.cc`) compared to PR #50787 and PR #51241:

- `Clang Tidy`:
  - 2-file C++ change (PR #51377 vs. PR #50787): **8m04s** (down from **15m32s**, **48% faster**). `bazel build` reuses the `cquery` analysis cache (analyzing in 0.8s-4.6s instead of 87s), deduplicates `scaled_dot_device_test` variants from 3 targets to 1, runs `ClangTidy` locally without the ~60s RBE upload stall, and runs `clang_tidy_diff.py` in 0.08s without a third Bazel invocation.
  - No C++ changes (PR #51376): **24s**.
- `DWYU (Depend on What You Use)`:
  - 2-file C++ change (PR #51377 vs. PR #50787): **1m53s** (down from **5m33s**, **66% faster**), analyzing 696 targets across the 2 modified packages in 96s instead of 15,729 targets across `//xla/...` in 202s.
  - No C++ changes (PR #51376 vs. PR #51241): **14s** (down from **5m18s**, **96% faster**).
- `Bazel Dependency Violations` (3 matrix jobs):
  - When build or `.bazelrc` files change (PR #51376 and PR #51377 vs. PR #50787): **3m19s-4m27s** (down from **6m28s-6m32s**, **32-49% faster**).
  - When no `BUILD`, `.bzl`, `WORKSPACE`, `MODULE.bazel`, or `.bazelrc` files change: skips `bazel cquery` in **~15s**.
- `Bazel Tags`: **1m04s-1m43s** (down from **3m18s** on PR #50787, **48-68% faster**).
- `Bazel Query`: **2m47s-3m12s** (down from **3m40s** on PR #50787, **13-24% faster**).

head_commit.message:
PR #49450: [ROCm] Autotune the MFMA instruction size for Triton GEMMs

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/49450

📝 Summary of Changes
Add `mfma_size` to the Triton GEMM config and autotune it on MFMA targets. MI300 default configs get `mfma_size: 16` variants. MI350 tries them only in exhaustive search.

🎯 Justification
The auto MFMA choice is often not the fastest on MI300.

🚀 Kind of Contribution:⚡️ Performance Improvement,

📊 Benchmark
  - MI300 wins: GPT-J 6B -12.9%, Flan-T5-L -9.7%, SDXL -6.5%, PaliGemma -5.5%.
Copybara import of the project:

--
263756c5777de795be80295c670e6b53a487dd56 by Aleksei Nurmukhametov <anurmukh@amd.com>:

[ROCm] Autotune the MFMA instruction size for Triton GEMMs

Triton picks the largest MFMA that fits the tile, which is not always
the fastest. Let the autotuner also try 16x16 MFMAs so it can pick
whichever is faster.

Tried by default on MI300 only. On MI350, it is limited to exhaustive
search. WMMA targets don't use MFMA.

Merging this change closes #49450

name: CI
display_title: Add the debug option `xla_gpu_experimental_enable_triton_scan` (default off). When it is set, `GpuCompiler` runs `ScanRewriterTriton` before `AssociativeScanRewriter`, so eligible associative `kScan` instructions become Triton scan fusions instead of reduce-window trees.

head_commit.message:
Add the debug option `xla_gpu_experimental_enable_triton_scan` (default off). When it is set, `GpuCompiler` runs `ScanRewriterTriton` before `AssociativeScanRewriter`, so eligible associative `kScan` instructions become Triton scan fusions instead of reduce-window trees.

The rewriter only sets the fusion kind to `__triton`; the tiling is chosen later by `PriorityFusion`, `FusionBlockLevelRewriter` or the autotuner.

Eligible scans have rank 1 or 2 with the scan dimension last, and the rewriter does nothing on GPUs that Triton does not support. A tiled scan computes one row per block, so scans with a dimension of at least 32768 also need at least 64 rows (`kMinParallelElements`); otherwise the hierarchical scan of `AssociativeScanRewriter` is faster (crossover at 64 rows on H100 and 32 on B200). Shorter scans are faster with Triton at any batch size.

For a cumsum with an elementwise epilogue on f32[B, N], with B from 1 to 256 and N from 1024 to 262144, enabling the flag is never slower on H100 and B200. It is 1.05–2.9x (H100) and 1.06–2.8x (B200) faster for N < 32768, and up to 1.9x (H100) and 2.3x (B200) faster for N ≥ 32768 and B ≥ 64.

A top-p sampling mask (softmax, cumsum, compare and select) on f32[B, K] with B from 1 to 256 and K in {64, 128} compiles to a single Triton kernel: 1.3–1.5 µs instead of 3.3–4.5 µs on H100, and 2.5–3.1 µs instead of 5.9–8.4 µs on B200.

display_title: Let PjRt OOM errors carry the reason why memory ran out.

head_commit.message:
Let PjRt OOM errors carry the reason why memory ran out.

`SetOomErrorWithPayload()` marks out-of-memory errors with an empty `pjrt.OOM` payload, so callers can tell that an operation ran out of memory, but not why: for example, whether the request was larger than the free memory or the free memory was too fragmented.

Add a required `OomReason` (`kOutOfMemory`, `kFragmentation` or `kUnknown`) to `SetOomErrorWithPayload()`, stored as the payload's value, and `GetOomErrorReason()` to read it back. `HasOomErrorPayload()` is unaffected.

display_title: [XLA] Memory-cost-aware latency hiding scheduler (kMemoryCost, aging, priced overlap)

head_commit.message:
[XLA] LHS: keep kMemoryCost off async starts and dones

Bottom-up, an async start looks like a pure releaser of the collective's
output, so kMemoryCost scored collective starts by bytes-per-cost and
reordered them. That is an overlap decision, not a memory one: it does not
change the peak by itself, but it perturbs the simulated timeline and can
flip downstream stall ties. On Qwen3-30B-A3B (GH200, 4-node AOT) one such
flip let the LM-head weight-gradient GEMM be used as overlap filler for a
tiny all-reduce after the backward loop, which kept the 5 GB logits gradient
live across the whole backward pass (+4.4 GB scheduler peak). Leaving async
starts and dones to the overlap rules restores the baseline schedule for
that model while keeping the rule's effect on compute releasers.

Adds AsyncStartsAreNotScored: with two independent all-gathers, the schedule
with the rule on must equal the one with it off.

Add the debug option `xla_gpu_experimental_enable_triton_scan` (default off). When it is set, `GpuCompiler` runs `ScanRewriterTriton` before `AssociativeScanRewriter`, so eligible associative `kScan` instructions become Triton scan fusions instead of reduce-window trees.

The rewriter only sets the fusion kind to `__triton`; the tiling is chosen later by `PriorityFusion`, `FusionBlockLevelRewriter` or the autotuner.

Eligible scans have rank 1 or 2 with the scan dimension last, and the rewriter does nothing on GPUs that Triton does not support. A tiled scan computes one row per block, so scans with a dimension of at least 32768 also need at least 64 rows (`kMinParallelElements`); otherwise the hierarchical scan of `AssociativeScanRewriter` is faster (crossover at 64 rows on H100 and 32 on B200). Shorter scans are faster with Triton at any batch size.

For a cumsum with an elementwise epilogue on f32[B, N], with B from 1 to 256 and N from 1024 to 262144, enabling the flag is never slower on H100 and B200. It is 1.05–2.9x (H100) and 1.06–2.8x (B200) faster for N < 32768, and up to 1.9x (H100) and 2.3x (B200) faster for N ≥ 32768 and B ≥ 64.

A top-p sampling mask (softmax, cumsum, compare and select) on f32[B, K] with B from 1 to 256 and K in {64, 128} compiles to a single Triton kernel: 1.3–1.5 µs instead of 3.3–4.5 µs on H100, and 2.5–3.1 µs instead of 5.9–8.4 µs on B200.

name: CI
display_title: Preserve `stack_frame_index` when embedding computations in `XlaBuilder`.

head_commit.message:
Preserve `stack_frame_index` when embedding computations in `XlaBuilder`.

`XlaBuilder::AddSubComputation` copied the embedded computation's
`HloComputationProto`s but dropped its `stack_frame_index`, leaving the
instructions' `stack_frame_id`s dangling. `HloModule::CanonicalizeStackFrameIds`
then reset them to 0, so source locations were lost for any computation built
via `ConvertMlirHloToHlo` and then embedded through `xla::Call`.

`XlaBuilder` now keeps a `StackFrames` table for imported computations:

-   `AddSubComputation` re-interns each imported frame (and its parent chain)
    into it, so identical frames are stored once, and rewrites the imported
    instructions' ids accordingly.
-   `BuildSubComputation` re-interns a child builder's table into its parent, only for entries that were imported with a stack frame index.
-   `Build()` / `BuildConstantSubGraph()` emit it as the module's
    `stack_frame_index`.
-   Ids set directly via `SetOpMetadata` (i.e. on the builder's own
    instructions, or on imported computations that carry no table) refer to a
    caller-owned table and are left untouched.

name: CI
display_title: Explicitly set infinite timeout on CoordinationServiceAgent CallOptions.

head_commit.message:
Explicitly set infinite timeout on CoordinationServiceAgent CallOptions.

When `CoordinationServiceAgent` issues long-running or unbounded RPCs (`PollForErrorAsync`, `WatchTasksAsync`, `GetKeyValueAsync`, and `WaitAtBarrierAsync`), it previously left `tsl::CallOptions` at its default timeout of `0`. Because `tsl::RPCState::StartCall` only sets a deadline on `grpc::ClientContext` when `timeout_in_ms_ > 0`, a default-constructed `grpc::ClientContext` can inherit an ambient context deadline instead of having no deadline.

Explicitly set `call_opts->SetTimeout(absl::ToInt64Milliseconds(absl::InfiniteDuration()))` on these `CallOptions` so `gpr_time_from_millis` translates `INT64_MAX` to `gpr_inf_future` and overrides any ambient deadline.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1004475848

concatenate operands.

name: CI
display_title: [XLA] Reverse kernel along reversed spatial dims in SimplifyConvToMultiply

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Reverse kernel along reversed spatial dims in SimplifyConvToMultiply

`AlgebraicSimplifierVisitor::SimplifyConvToMultiply` rewrites a convolution
whose spatial dimensions are all size 1 in either the kernel or the output into
a transpose, broadcast, multiply, and sum reduction. It previously ignored
`window_reversal` on the convolution window. When a contracted spatial dimension
has `window_reversal` set, the rewrite dropped the reversal and multiplied the
input by the unreversed kernel along that dimension. Reverse the kernel with
`MakeReverseHlo` along contracted spatial dimensions that have
`window_reversal` set before transposing and broadcasting.

name: CI
display_title: Replace 32x32 type-conversion expansion in `LiteralBase::Convert` with two-stage chunked canonical conversion.

head_commit.message:
Replace 32x32 type-conversion expansion in `LiteralBase::Convert` with two-stage chunked canonical conversion.

`LiteralBase::Convert` (`ConvertSwitch` in `xla/literal.cc`) previously nested `ArrayTypeSwitch` inside `ArrayTypeSwitch`, instantiating `32 x 32 = 1,024` `ConvertBetweenNativeTypes<NativeSrcT, NativeDestT>` conversion loops (~464 KB in `literal.pic.o`, mostly from inlining software-emulated narrow float `F4..BF16` and sub-byte integer `S1..U4` conversions across >600 type pairs). Replace the 2D template expansion with two sequential 1D `ArrayTypeSwitch` stages operating on 512-element stack chunks through canonical 64-bit integer (`uint64_t`) and `float`/`double` intermediate buffers (`f32_buf` for `F4..F32` and `f64_buf` when `F64` is involved, using `Eigen::half_impl::narrow_to_float` round-to-odd when narrowing `double` or 32/64-bit integers to `F4..BF16` to avoid double-rounding at midpoints):

```
// Before: 32 x 32 = 1,024 instantiated loop bodies
ArrayTypeSwitch(src_type):
  ArrayTypeSwitch(dst_type):
    ConvertBetweenNativeTypes<SrcT, DstT>(src, dst)

// After: 32 + 32 = 64 1D chunk stages over L1-resident stack buffers
for each 512-element chunk:
  ArrayTypeSwitch(src_type): unpack SrcT -> canonical int_buf / f32_buf / f64_buf
  if (src_is_int != dst_is_int || src_uses_f64 != dst_uses_f64): bridge buffers
  ArrayTypeSwitch(dst_type): pack canonical int_buf / f32_buf / f64_buf -> DstT
```

Runtime and memory performance impact:
- Heap memory overhead is zero (`int_buf`, `f32_buf`, and `f64_buf` use 10 KB of fixed stack storage in L1 cache, and `Literal result` is allocated only after validating `IsComplexType(src) && !IsComplexType(dst)`).
- CPU runtime has no regression; each software-emulated narrow float or sub-byte integer element is converted once in a tight 1D loop rather than re-converting narrow floats to both `double` and `float` inside float-to-int saturation checks.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1004429027

display_title: In `indexing_map.cc`, `SymbolicExprSimplifier::SimplifyAddConstraint` rewrote `a * gcd + b in [0, ub]` into `a * gcd in [0, ub]` whenever `([ub, ub] - range(b)).FloorDiv(gcd)` was a single point. That rewrite was unsound when `gcd` was negative or when `range(b)` did not share the same lower `CeilDiv(|gcd|)` quotient, and did not shift the bounds of `a * gcd` by `range(b)`.

head_commit.message:
In `indexing_map.cc`, `SymbolicExprSimplifier::SimplifyAddConstraint` rewrote `a * gcd + b in [0, ub]` into `a * gcd in [0, ub]` whenever `([ub, ub] - range(b)).FloorDiv(gcd)` was a single point. That rewrite was unsound when `gcd` was negative or when `range(b)` did not share the same lower `CeilDiv(|gcd|)` quotient, and did not shift the bounds of `a * gcd` by `range(b)`.

Simplify `a * gcd + b in [lb, ub]` to `a * gcd in [lb - b.lower, ub - b.upper]` when both `(lb - b)` under `CeilDiv(|gcd|)` and `(ub - b)` under `FloorDiv(|gcd|)` are single points, and decompose the constraint into `a * gcd == mul_val` and `b in [lb - mul_val, ub - mul_val]` whenever only a single multiple of `|gcd|` is feasible.

display_title: [XLA] Check element types for kConvert in FloatSupport::EffectiveOperandPrecisionIsOutputPrecision.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Check element types for kConvert in FloatSupport::EffectiveOperandPrecisionIsOutputPrecision.

Make `FloatSupport::EffectiveOperandPrecisionIsOutputPrecision` a `const` member method and restrict `HloOpcode::kConvert` to same-type converts or transitions between `low_precision_type_` and `high_precision_type_`. Previously `kConvert` unconditionally returned `true`, which treated narrowing or unrelated converts (such as `F32 -> S32` or `F32 -> F16` under `BF16`/`F32` propagation) as preserving operand precision.

Same-type `kConvert` (`in_type == out_type`) is explicitly allowed because `BFloat16Propagation::RunImpl` inserts temporary `F32 -> F32` `kConvert` copies on `kWhile` inputs before running dataflow analysis to break buffer aliasing with external users. During the forward and backward propagation passes, proposed `BF16` demotions are recorded in `changes_to_bf16_` while the HLO instructions themselves remain `F32 -> F32` in the module until `MaterializeResolvedPrecisions` and `SkipNoopConversions` run at the end of the pass, so `AllUsersConsumeBF16` and `AddEdgesForUse` require `EffectiveOperandPrecisionIsOutputPrecision` to return `true` on those same-type converts.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1004418610

display_title: In `indexing_map.cc`, `SymbolicExprSimplifier::SimplifyAddConstraint` rewrote `a * gcd + b in [0, ub]` into `a * gcd in [0, ub]` whenever `([ub, ub] - range(b)).FloorDiv(gcd)` was a single point. That rewrite was unsound when `gcd` was negative or when `range(b)` did not share the same lower `CeilDiv(|gcd|)` quotient, and did not shift the bounds of `a * gcd` by `range(b)`.

head_commit.message:
In `indexing_map.cc`, `SymbolicExprSimplifier::SimplifyAddConstraint` rewrote `a * gcd + b in [0, ub]` into `a * gcd in [0, ub]` whenever `([ub, ub] - range(b)).FloorDiv(gcd)` was a single point. That rewrite was unsound when `gcd` was negative or when `range(b)` did not share the same lower `CeilDiv(|gcd|)` quotient, and did not shift the bounds of `a * gcd` by `range(b)`.

Simplify `a * gcd + b in [lb, ub]` to `a * gcd in [lb - b.lower, ub - b.upper]` when both `(lb - b)` under `CeilDiv(|gcd|)` and `(ub - b)` under `FloorDiv(|gcd|)` are single points, and decompose the constraint into `a * gcd == mul_val` and `b in [lb - mul_val, ub - mul_val]` whenever only a single multiple of `|gcd|` is feasible.

name: CI
display_title: Explicitly set infinite timeout on CoordinationServiceAgent CallOptions.

head_commit.message:
Explicitly set infinite timeout on CoordinationServiceAgent CallOptions.

When `CoordinationServiceAgent` issues long-running or unbounded RPCs (`PollForErrorAsync`, `WatchTasksAsync`, `GetKeyValueAsync`, and `WaitAtBarrierAsync`), it previously left `tsl::CallOptions` at its default timeout of `0`. Because `tsl::RPCState::StartCall` only sets a deadline on `grpc::ClientContext` when `timeout_in_ms_ > 0`, a default-constructed `grpc::ClientContext` can inherit an ambient context deadline instead of having no deadline.

Explicitly set `call_opts->SetTimeout(absl::ToInt64Milliseconds(absl::InfiniteDuration()))` on these `CallOptions` so `gpr_time_from_millis` translates `INT64_MAX` to `gpr_inf_future` and overrides any ambient deadline.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1003605664
